{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122528Z-claude-with-skill-2/workspace/.claude/skills/security\n\n# Smart Contract Security\n\n## What You Probably Got Wrong\n\n**\"Solidity 0.8+ prevents overflows, so I'm safe.\"** Overflow is one of dozens of attack vectors. The big ones today: reentrancy, oracle manipulation, approval exploits, and decimal mishandling.\n\n**\"I tested it and it works.\"** Working correctly is not the same as being secure. Most exploits call functions in orders or with values the developer never considered.\n\n**\"It's a small contract, it doesn't need an audit.\"** The DAO hack was a simple reentrancy bug. The Euler exploit was a single missing check. Size doesn't correlate with safety.\n\n## Critical Vulnerabilities (With Defensive Code)\n\n### 1. Token Decimals Vary\n\n**USDC has 6 decimals, not 18.** This is the #1 source of \"where did my money go?\" bugs.\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ WRONG — assumes 18 decimals. Transfers 1 TRILLION USDC.\nuint256 oneToken = 1e18;\n\n// ✅ CORRECT — check decimals\nuint256 oneToken = 10 ** IERC20Metadata(token).decimals();\n```\n\nCommon decimals:\n| Token | Decimals |\n|-------|----------|\n| USDC, USDT | 6 |\n| WBTC | 8 |\n| DAI, WETH, most tokens | 18 |\n\n**When doing math across tokens with different decimals, normalize first:**\n```solidity\n// Converting USDC amount to 18-decimal internal accounting\nuint256 normalized = usdcAmount * 1e12; // 6 + 12 = 18 decimals\n```\n\n### 2. No Floating Point in Solidity\n\nSolidity has no `float` or `double`. Division truncates to zero.\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ WRONG — this equals 0\nuint256 fivePercent = 5 / 100;\n\n// ✅ CORRECT — basis points (1 bp = 0.01%)\nuint256 FEE_BPS = 500; // 5% = 500 basis points\nuint256 fee = (amount * FEE_BPS) / 10_000;\n```\n\n**Always multiply before dividing.** Division first = precision loss.\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ WRONG — loses precision\nuint256 result = a / b * c;\n\n// ✅ CORRECT — multiply first\nuint256 result = (a * c) / b;\n```\n\nFor complex math, use fixed-point libraries like `PRBMath` or `ABDKMath64x64`.\n\n### 3. Reentrancy\n\nAn external call can call back into your contract before the first call finishes. If you update state AFTER the external call, the attacker re-enters with stale state.\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ VULNERABLE — state updated after external call\nfunction withdraw() external {\n    uint256 bal = balances[msg.sender];\n    (bool success,) = msg.sender.call{value: bal}(\"\"); // ← attacker re-enters here\n    require(success);\n    balances[msg.sender] = 0; // Too late — attacker already withdrew again\n}\n\n// ✅ SAFE — Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern + reentrancy guard\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\n\nfunction withdraw() external nonReentrant {\n    uint256 bal = balances[msg.sender];\n    require(bal > 0, \"Nothing to withdraw\");\n    \n    balances[msg.sender] = 0;  // Effect BEFORE interaction\n    \n    (bool success,) = msg.sender.call{value: bal}(\"\");\n    require(success, \"Transfer failed\");\n}\n```\n\n**The pattern: Checks → Effects → Interactions (CEI)**\n1. **Checks** — validate inputs and conditions\n2. **Effects** — update all state\n3. **Interactions** — external calls last\n\nAlways use OpenZeppelin's `ReentrancyGuard` as a safety net on top of CEI.\n\n### 4. SafeERC20\n\nSome tokens (notably USDT) don't return `bool` on `transfer()` and `approve()`. Standard calls will revert even on success.\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ WRONG — breaks with USDT and other non-standard tokens\ntoken.transfer(to, amount);\ntoken.approve(spender, amount);\n\n// ✅ CORRECT — handles all token implementations\nimport {SafeERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/utils/SafeERC20.sol\";\nusing SafeERC20 for IERC20;\n\ntoken.safeTransfer(to, amount);\ntoken.safeApprove(spender, amount);\n```\n\n**Other token quirks to watch for:**\n- **Fee-on-transfer tokens:** Amount received < amount sent. Always check balance before and after.\n- **Rebasing tokens (stETH):** Balance changes without transfers. Use wrapped versions (wstETH).\n- **Pausable tokens (USDC):** Transfers can revert if the token is paused.\n- **Blocklist tokens (USDC, USDT):** Specific addresses can be blocked from transacting.\n\n### 5. Never Use DEX Spot Prices as Oracles\n\nA flash loan can manipulate any pool's spot price within a single transaction. This has caused hundreds of millions in losses.\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ DANGEROUS — manipulable in one transaction\nfunction getPrice() internal view returns (uint256) {\n    (uint112 reserve0, uint112 reserve1,) = uniswapPair.getReserves();\n    return (reserve1 * 1e18) / reserve0; // Spot price — easily manipulated\n}\n\n// ✅ SAFE — Chainlink with staleness + sanity checks\nfunction getPrice() internal view returns (uint256) {\n    (, int256 price,, uint256 updatedAt,) = priceFeed.latestRoundData();\n    require(block.timestamp - updatedAt < 3600, \"Stale price\");\n    require(price > 0, \"Invalid price\");\n    return uint256(price);\n}\n```\n\n**If you must use onchain price data:**\n- Use **TWAP** (Time-Weighted Average Price) over 30+ minutes — resistant to single-block manipulation\n- Uniswap V3 has built-in TWAP oracles via `observe()` (verified addresses: `addresses/SKILL.md`)\n- Still less safe than Chainlink for high-value decisions\n\n### 6. Vault Inflation Attack\n\nThe first depositor in an ERC-4626 vault can manipulate the share price to steal from subsequent depositors.\n\n**The attack:**\n1. Attacker deposits 1 wei → gets 1 share\n2. Attacker donates 1000 tokens directly to the vault (not via deposit)\n3. Now 1 share = 1001 tokens\n4. Victim deposits 1999 tokens → gets `1999 * 1 / 2000 = 0 shares` (rounds down)\n5. Attacker redeems 1 share → gets all 3000 tokens\n\n**The fix — virtual offset:**\n```solidity\nfunction convertToShares(uint256 assets) public view returns (uint256) {\n    return assets.mulDiv(\n        totalSupply() + 1e3,    // Virtual shares\n        totalAssets() + 1        // Virtual assets\n    );\n}\n```\n\nThe virtual offset makes the attack uneconomical — the attacker would need to donate enormous amounts to manipulate the ratio.\n\nOpenZeppelin's ERC4626 implementation includes this mitigation by default since v5.\n\n### 7. Infinite Approvals\n\n**Never use `type(uint256).max` as approval amount.**\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ DANGEROUS — if this contract is exploited, attacker drains your entire balance\ntoken.approve(someContract, type(uint256).max);\n\n// ✅ SAFE — approve only what's needed\ntoken.approve(someContract, exactAmountNeeded);\n\n// ✅ ACCEPTABLE — approve a small multiple for repeated interactions\ntoken.approve(someContract, amountPerTx * 5); // 5 transactions worth\n```\n\nIf a contract with infinite approval gets exploited (proxy upgrade bug, governance attack, undiscovered vulnerability), the attacker can drain every approved token from every user who granted unlimited access.\n\n### 8. Access Control\n\nEvery state-changing function needs explicit access control. \"Who should be able to call this?\" is the first question.\n\n```solidity\nimport {Ownable} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/access/Ownable.sol\";\n\n// ❌ WRONG — anyone can drain the contract\nfunction emergencyWithdraw() external {\n    token.transfer(msg.sender, token.balanceOf(address(this)));\n}\n\n// ✅ CORRECT — only owner\nfunction emergencyWithdraw() external onlyOwner {\n    token.transfer(owner(), token.balanceOf(address(this)));\n}\n```\n\nFor complex permissions, use OpenZeppelin's `AccessControl` with role-based separation (ADMIN_ROLE, OPERATOR_ROLE, etc.).\n\n### 9. Input Validation\n\nNever trust inputs. Validate everything.\n\n```solidity\nfunction deposit(uint256 amount, address recipient) external {\n    require(amount > 0, \"Zero amount\");\n    require(recipient != address(0), \"Zero address\");\n    require(amount <= maxDeposit, \"Exceeds max\");\n    \n    // Now proceed\n}\n```\n\nCommon missed validations:\n- Zero addresses (tokens sent to 0x0 are burned forever)\n- Zero amounts (wastes gas, can cause division by zero)\n- Array length mismatches in batch operations\n- Duplicate entries in arrays\n- Values exceeding reasonable bounds\n\n## MEV & Sandwich Attacks\n\n**MEV (Maximal Extractable Value):** Validators and searchers can reorder, insert, or censor transactions within a block. They profit by frontrunning your transaction, backrunning it, or both.\n\n### Sandwich Attacks\n\nThe most common MEV attack on DeFi users:\n\n```\n1. You submit: swap 10 ETH → USDC on Uniswap (slippage 1%)\n2. Attacker sees your tx in the mempool\n3. Attacker frontruns: buys USDC before you → price rises\n4. Your swap executes at a worse price (but within your 1% slippage)\n5. Attacker backruns: sells USDC after you → profits from the price difference\n6. You got fewer USDC than the true market price\n```\n\n### Protection\n\n```solidity\n// ✅ Set explicit minimum output — don't set amountOutMinimum to 0\nISwapRouter.ExactInputSingleParams memory params = ISwapRouter\n    .ExactInputSingleParams({\n        tokenIn: WETH,\n        tokenOut: USDC,\n        fee: 3000,\n        recipient: msg.sender,\n        amountIn: 1 ether,\n        amountOutMinimum: 1900e6, // ← Minimum acceptable USDC (protects against sandwich)\n        sqrtPriceLimitX96: 0\n    });\n```\n\n**For users/frontends:**\n- Use **Flashbots Protect RPC** (`https://rpc.flashbots.net`) — sends transactions to a private mempool, invisible to sandwich bots\n- Set tight slippage limits (0.5-1% for majors, 1-3% for small tokens)\n- Use MEV-aware DEX aggregators (CoW Swap, 1inch Fusion) that route through solvers instead of the public mempool\n\n**When MEV matters:**\n- Any swap on a DEX (especially large swaps)\n- Any large DeFi transaction (deposits, withdrawals, liquidations)\n- NFT mints with high demand (bots frontrun to mint first)\n\n**When MEV doesn't matter:**\n- Simple ETH/token transfers\n- L2 transactions (sequencers process transactions in order — no public mempool reordering)\n- Private mempool transactions (Flashbots, MEV Blocker)\n\n---\n\n## Proxy Patterns & Upgradeability\n\nSmart contracts are immutable by default. Proxies let you upgrade the logic while keeping the same address and state.\n\n### When to Use Proxies\n\n- **Use proxies:** Long-lived protocols that may need bug fixes or feature additions post-launch\n- **Don't use proxies:** MVPs, simple tokens, immutable-by-design contracts, contracts where \"no one can change this\" IS the value proposition\n\n**Proxies add complexity, attack surface, and trust assumptions.** Users must trust that the admin won't upgrade to a malicious implementation. Don't use proxies just because you can.\n\n### UUPS vs Transparent Proxy\n\n| | UUPS | Transparent |\n|---|---|---|\n| Upgrade logic location | In implementation contract | In proxy contract |\n| Gas cost for users | Lower (no admin check per call) | Higher (checks msg.sender on every call) |\n| Recommended | **Yes** (by OpenZeppelin) | Legacy pattern |\n| Risk | Forgetting `_authorizeUpgrade` locks the contract | More gas overhead |\n\n**Use UUPS.** It's cheaper, simpler, and what OpenZeppelin recommends.\n\n### UUPS Implementation\n\n```solidity\n// Implementation contract (the logic)\nimport {UUPSUpgradeable} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/proxy/utils/UUPSUpgradeable.sol\";\nimport {Initializable} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/proxy/utils/Initializable.sol\";\nimport {OwnableUpgradeable} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/access/OwnableUpgradeable.sol\";\n\ncontract MyContractV1 is Initializable, UUPSUpgradeable, OwnableUpgradeable {\n    uint256 public value;\n\n    /// @custom:oz-upgrades-unsafe-allow constructor\n    constructor() {\n        _disableInitializers(); // Prevent implementation from being initialized\n    }\n\n    function initialize(address owner) public initializer {\n        __Ownable_init(owner);\n        __UUPSUpgradeable_init();\n        value = 42;\n    }\n\n    function _authorizeUpgrade(address) internal override onlyOwner {}\n}\n```\n\n### Critical Rules\n\n1. **Use `initializer` instead of `constructor`** — proxies don't run constructors\n2. **Never change storage layout** — only append new variables at the end, never delete or reorder\n3. **Use OpenZeppelin's upgradeable contracts** — `@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable`, not `@openzeppelin/contracts`\n4. **Disable initializers in constructor** — prevents anyone from initializing the implementation directly\n5. **Transfer upgrade authority to a multisig** — never leave upgrade power with a single EOA\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ WRONG — reordering storage breaks everything\n// V1: uint256 a; uint256 b;\n// V2: uint256 b; uint256 a;  ← Swapped! 'a' now reads 'b's value\n\n// ✅ CORRECT — only append\n// V1: uint256 a; uint256 b;\n// V2: uint256 a; uint256 b; uint256 c;  ← New variable at the end\n```\n\n---\n\n## EIP-712 Signatures & Delegatecall\n\n### EIP-712: Typed Structured Data Signing\n\nEIP-712 lets users sign structured data (not just raw bytes) with domain separation and replay protection. Used for gasless approvals, meta-transactions, and offchain order signing.\n\n**When to use:**\n- **Permit (ERC-2612)** — gasless token approvals (user signs, anyone can submit)\n- **Offchain orders** — sign buy/sell orders offchain, settle onchain (0x, Seaport)\n- **Meta-transactions** — user signs intent, relayer submits and pays gas\n\n```solidity\n// EIP-712 domain separator — prevents replay across contracts and chains\nbytes32 public constant DOMAIN_TYPEHASH = keccak256(\n    \"EIP712Domain(string name,string version,uint256 chainId,address verifyingContract)\"\n);\n\nbytes32 public constant PERMIT_TYPEHASH = keccak256(\n    \"Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)\"\n);\n\nfunction permit(\n    address owner, address spender, uint256 value,\n    uint256 deadline, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s\n) external {\n    require(block.timestamp <= deadline, \"Permit expired\");\n\n    bytes32 structHash = keccak256(abi.encode(\n        PERMIT_TYPEHASH, owner, spender, value, nonces[owner]++, deadline\n    ));\n    bytes32 digest = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(\n        \"\\x19\\x01\", DOMAIN_SEPARATOR(), structHash\n    ));\n\n    address recovered = ecrecover(digest, v, r, s);\n    require(recovered == owner, \"Invalid signature\");\n\n    _approve(owner, spender, value);\n}\n```\n\n**Key properties:**\n- **Domain separator** prevents replaying signatures on different contracts or chains\n- **Nonce** prevents replaying the same signature twice\n- **Deadline** prevents stale signatures from being used later\n- In practice, use OpenZeppelin's `EIP712` and `ERC20Permit` — don't implement from scratch\n\n### Delegatecall\n\n`delegatecall` executes another contract's code in the caller's storage context. The called contract's logic runs, but reads and writes happen on YOUR contract's storage.\n\n**This is extremely dangerous if the target is untrusted.**\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ CRITICAL VULNERABILITY — delegatecall to user-supplied address\nfunction execute(address target, bytes calldata data) external {\n    target.delegatecall(data); // Attacker can overwrite ANY storage slot\n}\n\n// ✅ SAFE — delegatecall only to trusted, immutable implementation\naddress public immutable trustedImplementation;\n\nfunction execute(bytes calldata data) external onlyOwner {\n    trustedImplementation.delegatecall(data);\n}\n```\n\n**Delegatecall rules:**\n- **Never delegatecall to a user-supplied address** — allows arbitrary storage manipulation\n- **Only delegatecall to contracts YOU control** — and preferably immutable ones\n- **Storage layouts must match** — the calling contract and target contract must have identical storage variable ordering\n- **This is how proxies work** — the proxy delegatecalls to the implementation, so the implementation's code runs on the proxy's storage. That's why storage layout matters so much for upgradeable contracts.\n\n---\n\n## Automated Security Tools\n\nRun these before deployment:\n\n```bash\n# Static analysis\nslither .                     # Detects common vulnerabilities\nmythril analyze Contract.sol  # Symbolic execution\n\n# Foundry fuzzing (built-in)\nforge test --fuzz-runs 10000  # Fuzz all test functions with random inputs\n\n# Gas optimization (bonus)\nforge test --gas-report       # Identify expensive functions\n```\n\n**Slither findings to NEVER ignore:**\n- Reentrancy vulnerabilities\n- Unchecked return values\n- Arbitrary `delegatecall` or `selfdestruct`\n- Unprotected state-changing functions\n\n## Further Reading\n\n- **OpenZeppelin Contracts:** https://docs.openzeppelin.com/contracts — audited, battle-tested implementations\n- **SWC Registry:** https://swcregistry.io — comprehensive vulnerability catalog\n- **Rekt News:** https://rekt.news — real exploit post-mortems\n- **SpeedRun Ethereum:** https://speedrunethereum.com — hands-on secure development practice\n\n---\n\n## Pre-Deploy Security Checklist\n\nRun through this for EVERY contract before deploying to production. No exceptions.\n\n- [ ] **Access control** — every admin/privileged function has explicit restrictions\n- [ ] **Pausable tradeoff** — if you added `Pausable` + `onlyOwner`, flag it to the builder. A single key that can freeze all users is a censorship vector. Suggest timelocks or multisig governance.\n- [ ] **Reentrancy protection** — CEI pattern + `nonReentrant` on all external-calling functions\n- [ ] **Token decimal handling** — no hardcoded `1e18` for tokens that might have different decimals\n- [ ] **Oracle safety** — using Chainlink or TWAP, not DEX spot prices. Staleness checks present\n- [ ] **Integer math** — multiply before divide. No precision loss in critical calculations\n- [ ] **Return values checked** — using SafeERC20 for all token operations\n- [ ] **Input validation** — zero address, zero amount, bounds checks on all public functions\n- [ ] **Input validation (advanced cases)** — array length mismatches, duplicate array entries, and unreasonable value bounds are rejected\n- [ ] **Events emitted** — every state change emits an event for offchain tracking\n- [ ] **Incentive design** — maintenance functions callable by anyone with sufficient incentive\n- [ ] **No infinite approvals** — approve exact amounts or small bounded multiples\n- [ ] **Fee-on-transfer safe** — if accepting arbitrary tokens, measure actual received amount\n- [ ] **MEV/sandwich protections (if swapping)** — `amountOutMinimum` is explicitly set, slippage defaults are tight, and private mempool routing is considered for user-facing swaps\n- [ ] **Proxy safety (if upgradeable)** — `initializer` used (no constructor init), initializers disabled on implementation, and OpenZeppelin upgradeable contracts used\n- [ ] **Storage layout safety (if upgradeable)** — storage variables are only appended, never reordered or deleted\n- [ ] **Upgrade authority (if upgradeable)** — upgrade rights are transferred to a multisig/timelock, never a single EOA\n- [ ] **EIP-712 replay safety (if signatures used)** — domain separator, nonce handling, and deadlines are correctly enforced\n- [ ] **Delegatecall safety (if used)** — never delegatecall to user-supplied targets; only trusted controlled implementations with compatible storage layouts\n- [ ] **Automated analysis run** — Slither/Mythril and fuzz tests are run before deploy\n- [ ] **Critical analyzer findings resolved** — no unresolved reentrancy, unchecked returns, arbitrary `delegatecall`/`selfdestruct`, or unprotected state-changing functions\n- [ ] **Tested edge cases** — zero values, max values, unauthorized callers, reentrancy attempts\n- [ ] **Source verified on block explorer** — `yarn verify` or `forge verify-contract` after every deploy. Unverified contracts can't be audited by users and look indistinguishable from scams\n\n---\n\nBefore you finish: send a one-line note via [feedback/SKILL.md](https://ethskills.com/feedback/SKILL.md) — issue or praise.\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"78210e2d-ae8e-4bb2-a869-e8efb63e9f6d","uuid":"ce8f28dc-03e1-425c-a89f-38bfe295b50f","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:25:33.028Z","isSynthetic":true}

 function withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner) public virtual returns (uint256) {\n198\t        uint256 maxAssets = maxWithdraw(owner);\n199\t        if (assets > maxAssets) (uint256) {\n        return _convertToAssets(shares, Math.Rounding.Floor);\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IERC4626\n    function maxDeposit(address) public view virtual returns (uint256) {\n        return type(uint256).max;\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IERC4626\n    function maxMint(address) public view virtual returns (uint256) {\n        return type(uint256).max;\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IERC4626\n    function maxWithdraw(address owner) public view virtual returns (uint256) {\n        return _convertToAssets(balanceOf(owner), Math.Rounding.Floor);\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IERC4626\n    function maxRedeem(address owner) public view virtual returns (uint256) {\n        return balanceOf(owner);\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IERC4626\n    function previewDeposit(uint256 assets) public view virtual returns (uint256) {\n        return _convertToShares(assets, Math.Rounding.Floor);\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IERC4626\n    function previewMint(uint256 shares) public view virtual returns (uint256) {\n        return _convertToAssets(shares, Math.Rounding.Ceil);\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IERC4626\n    function previewWithdraw(uint256 assets) public view virtual returns (uint256) {\n        return _convertToShares(assets, Math.Rounding.Ceil);\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IERC4626\n    function previewRedeem(uint256 shares) public view virtual returns (uint256) {\n        return _convertToAssets(shares, Math.Rounding.Floor);\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IERC4626\n    function deposit(uint256 assets, address receiver) public virtual returns (uint256) {\n        uint256 maxAssets = maxDeposit(receiver);\n        if (assets > maxAssets) {\n            revert ERC4626ExceededMaxDeposit(receiver, assets, maxAssets);\n        }\n\n        uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets);\n        _deposit(_msgSender(), receiver, assets, shares);\n\n        return shares;\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IERC4626\n    function mint(uint256 shares, address receiver) public virtual returns (uint256) {\n        uint256 maxShares = maxMint(receiver);\n        if (shares > maxShares) {\n            revert ERC4626ExceededMaxMint(receiver, shares, maxShares);\n        }\n\n        uint256 assets = previewMint(shares);\n        _deposit(_msgSender(), receiver, assets, shares);\n\n        return assets;\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IERC4626\n    function withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner) public virtual returns (uint256) {\n        uint256 maxAssets = maxWithdraw(owner);\n        if (assets > maxAssets) {\n            revert ERC4626ExceededMaxWithdraw(owner, assets, maxAssets);\n        }\n\n        uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets);\n        _withdraw(_msgSender(), receiver, owner, assets, shares);\n\n        return shares;\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IERC4626\n    function redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address owner) public virtual returns (uint256) {\n        uint256 maxShares = maxRedeem(owner);\n        if (shares > maxShares) {\n            revert ERC4626ExceededMaxRedeem(owner, shares, maxShares);\n        }\n\n        uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares);\n        _withdraw(_msgSender(), receiver, owner, assets, shares);\n\n        return assets;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Internal conversion function (from assets to shares) with support for rounding direction.\n     */\n    function _convertToShares(uint256 assets, Math.Rounding rounding) internal view virtual returns (uint256) {\n        return assets.mulDiv(totalSupply() + 10 ** _decimalsOffset(), totalAssets() + 1, rounding);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Internal conversion function (from shares to assets) with support for rounding direction.\n     */\n    function _convertToAssets(uint256 shares, Math.Rounding rounding) internal view virtual returns (uint256) {\n        return shares.mulDiv(totalAssets() + 1, totalSupply() + 10 ** _decimalsOffset(), rounding);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Deposit/mint common workflow.\n     */\n    function _deposit(address caller, address receiver, uint256 assets, uint256 shares) internal virtual {\n        // If asset() is ERC-777, `transferFrom` can trigger a reentrancy BEFORE the transfer happens through the\n        // `tokensToSend` hook. On the other hand, the `tokenReceived` hook, that is triggered after the transfer,\n        // calls the vault, which is assumed not malicious.\n        //\n        // Conclusion: we need to do the transfer before we mint so that any reentrancy would happen before the\n        // assets are transferred and before the shares are minted, which is a valid state.\n        // slither-disable-next-line reentrancy-no-eth\n        SafeERC20.safeTransferFrom(IERC20(asset()), caller, address(this), assets);\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n\n        emit Deposit(caller, receiver, assets, shares);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Withdraw/redeem common workflow.\n     */\n    function _withdraw(\n        address caller,\n        address receiver,\n        address owner,\n        uint256 assets,\n        uint256 shares\n    ) internal virtual {\n        if (caller != owner) {\n            _spendAllowance(owner, caller, shares);\n        }\n\n        // If asset() is ERC-777, `transfer` can trigger a reentrancy AFTER the transfer happens through the\n        // `tokensReceived` hook. On the other hand, the `tokensToSend` hook, that is triggered before the transfer,\n        // calls the vault, which is assumed not malicious.\n        //\n        // Conclusion: we need to do the transfer after the burn so that any reentrancy would happen after the\n        // shares are burned and after the assets are transferred, which is a valid state.\n        _burn(owner, shares);\n        SafeERC20.safeTransfer(IERC20(asset()), receiver, assets);\n\n        emit Withdraw(caller, receiver, owner, assets, shares);\n    }\n\n    function _decimalsOffset() internal view virtual returns (uint8) {\n        return 0;\n    }\n}\n","numLines":174,"startLine":110,"totalLines":283}}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTfNhLr4XNC1dE8cvzK","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01CDgRHV62b6n6T299wVKsAy","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122528Z-claude-with-skill-2/workspace/src/libraries/TokenMetadata.sol","content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\n/**\n * @title TokenMetadata\n * @notice Reads `symbol()` / `decimals()` off an arbitrary ERC-20 without ever reverting.\n *\n * @dev Listing is permissionless, so the token we are asked to wrap may be non-conforming:\n *      - no `symbol()` at all (early tokens),\n *      - `symbol()` returning `bytes32` instead of `string` (MKR),\n *      - `symbol()` returning garbage / oversized / unprintable data.\n *\n *      We use raw `staticcall` + manual decoding rather than `try/catch`, because `abi.decode`\n *      of malformed return data reverts in the *caller's* frame and would brick vault creation.\n *      Symbols are sanitised to printable ASCII and capped, so a token cannot inject control\n *      characters or a 10kB blob into the receipt token's metadata.\n */\nlibrary TokenMetadata {\n    /// @dev Symbols longer than this are truncated. Real symbols are <= ~11 chars.\n    uint256 private constant MAX_SYMBOL_BYTES = 32;\n\n    /// @dev Matches OpenZeppelin's ERC4626 fallback when `decimals()` is unreadable.\n    uint8 internal constant DEFAULT_DECIMALS = 18;\n\n    /// @notice Name for the receipt token of a vault holding `token`.\n    function vaultName(address token) internal view returns (string memory) {\n        return string.concat(\"Saved \", _symbolOr(token, \"Token\"));\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Symbol for the receipt token of a vault holding `token`.\n    /// @dev Not unique: two different tokens may report the same symbol. Index by vault address.\n    function vaultSymbol(address token) internal view returns (string memory) {\n        return string.concat(\"sv\", _symbolOr(token, \"TKN\"));\n    }\n\n    /// @notice `token.decimals()`, or `DEFAULT_DECIMALS` if the call fails or is malformed.\n    function safeDecimals(address token) internal view returns (uint8) {\n        (bool ok, bytes memory ret) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSignature(\"decimals()\"));\n        if (!ok || ret.length != 32) return DEFAULT_DECIMALS;\n        uint256 value = abi.decode(ret, (uint256));\n        if (value > type(uint8).max) return DEFAULT_DECIMALS;\n        return uint8(value);\n    }\n\n    function _symbolOr(address token, string memory fallbackSymbol) private view returns (string memory) {\n        string memory symbol_ = _readString(token, abi.encodeWithSignature(\"symbol()\"));\n        return bytes(symbol_).length == 0 ? fallbackSymbol : symbol_;\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Returns \"\" for any return shape we do not fully understand.\n    function _readString(address token, bytes memory callData) private view returns (string memory) {\n        (bool ok, bytes memory ret) = token.staticcall(callData);\n        if (!ok) return \"\";\n\n        if (ret.length == 32) {\n            // bytes32-style metadata (MKR and other pre-standard tokens).\n            return _sanitize(_unpackBytes32(abi.decode(ret, (bytes32))));\n        }\n\n        // ABI-encoded string: [offset][length][data...]. Reject anything not in canonical form.\n        if (ret.length < 64) return \"\";\n        uint256 offset = _word(ret, 0);\n        if (offset != 32) return \"\";\n        uint256 length = _word(ret, 32);\n        if (length == 0 || 64 + length > ret.length) return \"\";\n        if (length > MAX_SYMBOL_BYTES) length = MAX_SYMBOL_BYTES;\n\n        bytes memory raw = new bytes(length);\n        for (uint256 i; i < length; ++i) {\n            raw[i] = ret[64 + i];\n        }\n        return _sanitize(raw);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Keeps printable ASCII only; drops control characters and multi-byte sequences.\n    function _sanitize(bytes memory raw) private pure returns (string memory) {\n        bytes memory out = new bytes(raw.length);\n        uint256 n;\n        for (uint256 i; i < raw.length; ++i) {\n            uint8 c = uint8(raw[i]);\n            if (c >= 0x20 && c <= 0x7E) {\n                out[n++] = raw[i];\n            }\n        }\n        assembly (\"memory-safe\") {\n            mstore(out, n)\n        }\n        return string(out);\n    }\n\n    function _unpackBytes32(bytes32 value) private pure returns (bytes memory) {\n        uint256 length;\n        while (length < 32 && value[length] != 0) {\n            ++length;\n        }\n        bytes memory out = new bytes(length);\n        for (uint256 i; i < length; ++i) {\n            out[i] = value[i];\n        }\n        return out;\n    }\n\n    function _word(bytes memory data, uint256 offset) private pure returns (uint256 value) {\n        assembly (\"memory-safe\") {\n            value := mload(add(data, add(32, offset)))\n        }\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":409,"cache_read_input_tokens":57089,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":409},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"78210e2d-ae8e-4bb2-a869-e8efb63e9f6d","uuid":"a2d850ff-6a9d-4531-b34a-5a14e239ca2c","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:32:30.831Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTfMQCnFxa6EEkjuq9f"}

Reject anything not in canonical form.\n        if (ret.length < 64) return \"\";\n        uint256 offset = _word(ret, 0);\n        if (offset != 32) return \"\";\n        uint256 length = _word(ret, 32);\n        if (length == 0 || 64 + length > ret.length) return \"\";\n        if (length > MAX_SYMBOL_BYTES) length = MAX_SYMBOL_BYTES;\n\n        bytes memory raw = new bytes(length);\n        for (uint256 i; i < length; ++i) {\n            raw[i] = ret[64 + i];\n        }\n        return _sanitize(raw);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Keeps printable ASCII only; drops control characters and multi-byte sequences.\n    function _sanitize(bytes memory raw) private pure returns (string memory) {\n        bytes memory out = new bytes(raw.length);\n        uint256 n;\n        for (uint256 i; i < raw.length; ++i) {\n            uint8 c = uint8(raw[i]);\n            if (c >= 0x20 && c <= 0x7E) {\n                out[n++] = raw[i];\n            }\n        }\n        assembly (\"memory-safe\") {\n            mstore(out, n)\n        }\n        return string(out);\n    }\n\n    function _unpackBytes32(bytes32 value) private pure returns (bytes memory) {\n        uint256 length;\n        while (length < 32 && value[length] != 0) {\n            ++length;\n        }\n        bytes memory out = new bytes(length);\n        for (uint256 i; i < length; ++i) {\n            out[i] = value[i];\n        }\n        return out;\n    }\n\n    function _word(bytes memory data, uint256 offset) private pure returns (uint256 value) {\n        assembly (\"memory-safe\") {\n            value := mload(add(data, add(32, offset)))\n        }\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}

Depositors get a transferable ERC-4626\n *         receipt token representing a pro-rata claim on everything the vault holds.\n *\n * @dev Accounting model\n *      ------------------\n *      `totalAssets()` is the vault's live balance of the underlying, NOT an internal counter.\n *      That is what makes \"the keeper just sends tokens in\" work: a plain `transfer` into this\n *      contract raises `totalAssets()` without minting shares, so every share is instantly worth\n *      more. There is no `accrue()` to call, no reward index, and no per-user bookkeeping.\n *\n *      The flip side of balance-based accounting is that a *donation* is indistinguishable from\n *      yield, which is the classic ERC-4626 inflation attack. That is handled with a virtual\n *      share/asset offset of 1e6 (see `_decimalsOffset`), not by trying to detect donations.\n *\n * @dev Trust model\n *      -----------\n *      This vault is ownerless and immutable: no admin, no pause, no upgrade, no rescue function.\n *      Nobody — including the deployer — can freeze deposits, change the fee (there is none), or\n *      move user funds. The cost of that choice is that there is also no emergency stop if the\n *      *underlying* token turns out to be malicious. Listing a token is not an endorsement of it;\n *      the risk of the asset stays with the depositor. See NOTES.md.\n */\ncontract SaveVault is ERC4626, ReentrancyGuard {\n    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;\n    using Math for uint256;\n\n    /// @dev Virtual shares/assets exponent. Makes the first-depositor inflation attack cost\n    ///      ~1e6x the profit it could extract, which prices it out entirely.\n    uint8 private constant DECIMALS_OFFSET = 6;\n\n    /// @dev `decimals()` returns `assetDecimals + DECIMALS_OFFSET` as a uint8, so an absurd\n    ///      underlying would permanently revert it. Reject at construction instead.\n    uint8 internal constant MAX_ASSET_DECIMALS = 36;\n\n    /// @notice Factory that deployed this vault (address(0) if deployed standalone).\n    address public immutable factory;\n\n    /// @notice Emitted when yield is pushed in through `donate`. Plain transfers into the vault\n    ///         also count as yield but cannot emit an event — index `totalAssets()` for those.\n    event YieldAdded(address indexed from, uint256 amount, uint256 newTotalAssets);\n\n    error ZeroAmount();\n    error ZeroShares();\n    error ZeroAssets();\n    error ZeroAddress();\n    error UnsupportedDecimals(uint8 assetDecimals);\n    error InexactMint(uint256 requested, uint256 received);\n    error NoSharesOutstanding();\n\n    constructor(IERC20 asset_)\n        ERC20(TokenMetadata.vaultName(address(asset_)), TokenMetadata.vaultSymbol(address(asset_)))\n        ERC4626(asset_)\n    {\n        uint8 assetDecimals = TokenMetadata.safeDecimals(address(asset_));\n        if (assetDecimals > MAX_ASSET_DECIMALS) revert UnsupportedDecimals(assetDecimals);\n        factory = msg.sender;\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Deposits\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Deposit `assets` of the underlying and receive receipt shares.\n     * @dev Shares are minted against the amount the vault *actually received*, priced at the\n     *      share ratio from *before* the transfer. Both matter:\n     *      - fee-on-transfer tokens deliver less than `assets`; minting on the requested amount\n     *        would hand out unbacked shares and dilute existing holders;\n     *      - pricing after the transfer would let the depositor's own assets inflate the\n     *        denominator and shortchange them.\n     *      Consequence: for fee-on-transfer tokens the return value can be lower than\n     *      `previewDeposit(assets)`. That is a deliberate deviation from the ERC-4626 preview\n     *      guarantee; the alternative is silently socialising the fee onto existing depositors.\n     */\n    function deposit(uint256 assets, address receiver) public override nonReentrant returns (uint256 shares) {\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        (, shares) = _pullAndMint(assets, receiver);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Mint exactly `shares` receipt tokens, pulling however much underlying that costs.\n     * @dev Reverts for fee-on-transfer tokens: \"exactly `shares`\" cannot be honoured when the\n     *      transferred amount arrives short. Use `deposit` for those tokens.\n     */\n    function mint(uint256 shares, address receiver) public override nonReentrant returns (uint256 assets) {\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        assets = previewMint(shares); // rounds up, in the vault's favour\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        (uint256 received, uint256 mintedShares) = _pullAndMint(assets, receiver);\n        if (received != assets || mintedShares != shares) revert InexactMint(shares, mintedShares);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Withdrawals\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice Burn shares to withdraw exactly `assets` of the underlying.\n    /// @dev Fee-on-transfer tokens: the vault sends `assets`, `receiver` may net less.\n    function withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner)\n        public\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256 shares)\n    {\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n        shares = super.withdraw(assets, receiver, owner);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Burn exactly `shares` and withdraw the underlying they are worth.\n    function redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address owner)\n        public\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256 assets)\n    {\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n        assets = super.redeem(shares, receiver, owner);\n        // Dust redemptions that round to nothing would burn shares for free.\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAssets();\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Yield\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Push `amount` of the underlying in as yield, lifting every holder's claim.\n     * @dev Permissionless by design — the keeper needs no privileges, and anyone topping the\n     *      vault up only benefits existing holders. Functionally identical to transferring the\n     *      tokens in directly; this path just measures the real amount received and emits an\n     *      event, which is what the keeper should use so its deliveries are indexable.\n     */\n    function donate(uint256 amount) external nonReentrant {\n        if (amount == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        // With no shares outstanding there is nobody to credit, and the donation would instead\n        // wreck the share price for the next depositor.\n        if (totalSupply() == 0) revert NoSharesOutstanding();\n\n        IERC20 asset_ = IERC20(asset());\n        uint256 balanceBefore = asset_.balanceOf(address(this));\n        asset_.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\n        uint256 balanceAfter = asset_.balanceOf(address(this));\n\n        emit YieldAdded(msg.sender, balanceAfter - balanceBefore, balanceAfter);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Views\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /**\n     * @notice True while a deposit/withdraw is mid-flight inside this vault.\n     * @dev Integrators pricing this vault from inside an ERC-777/callback hook must check this.\n     *      During `deposit` the underlying has already landed but the shares are not minted yet,\n     *      so `convertToAssets` reads high for the duration of the callback. Read-only\n     *      reentrancy is not a reentrancy bug in this contract, it is a hazard for readers.\n     */\n    function isEntered() external view returns (bool) {\n        return _reentrancyGuardEntered();\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Internals\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function _decimalsOffset() internal pure override returns (uint8) {\n        return DECIMALS_OFFSET;\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Checks-effects-interactions cannot fully apply here: the amount received is only\n    ///      knowable after the transfer. `nonReentrant` on every entry point is what keeps the\n    ///      window safe, and the balance delta is read fresh rather than assumed.\n    function _pullAndMint(uint256 assets, address receiver) private returns (uint256 received, uint256 shares) {\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n\n        IERC20 asset_ = IERC20(asset());\n        uint256 totalAssetsBefore = asset_.balanceOf(address(this));\n        uint256 totalSupplyBefore = totalSupply();\n\n        asset_.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), assets);\n\n        // Reverts on underflow if the token somehow reduced our balance.\n        received = asset_.balanceOf(address(this)) - totalAssetsBefore;\n        if (received == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        // Same formula as ERC4626._convertToShares, evaluated at the pre-transfer state.\n        shares = received.mulDiv(totalSupplyBefore + 10 ** DECIMALS_OFFSET, totalAssetsBefore + 1, Math.Rounding.Floor);\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroShares();\n\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n        emit Deposit(msg.sender, receiver, received, shares);\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2056,"cache_read_input_tokens":57498,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2056},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"78210e2d-ae8e-4bb2-a869-e8efb63e9f6d","uuid":"df0a9fa6-27bf-4678-b43b-be865d7364b7","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:33:16.090Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTgtw3jZKMuW7R4zox1"}

Use `deposit` for those tokens.\n     */\n    function mint(uint256 shares, address receiver) public override nonReentrant returns (uint256 assets) {\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        assets = previewMint(shares); // rounds up, in the vault's favour\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        (uint256 received, uint256 mintedShares) = _pullAndMint(assets, receiver);\n        if (received != assets || mintedShares != shares) revert InexactMint(shares, mintedShares);\n    }","newString":"    function deposit(uint256 assets, address receiver) public override nonReentrant returns (uint256 shares) {\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n\n        uint256 totalSupplyBefore = totalSupply();\n        (uint256 totalAssetsBefore, uint256 received) = _pull(assets);\n        if (received == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        // Same formula as ERC4626._convertToShares, evaluated at the pre-transfer state.\n        shares = received.mulDiv(totalSupplyBefore + 10 ** DECIMALS_OFFSET, totalAssetsBefore + 1, Math.Rounding.Floor);\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroShares();\n\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n        emit Deposit(msg.sender, receiver, received, shares);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Mint exactly `shares` receipt tokens, pulling however much underlying that costs.\n     * @dev Reverts for fee-on-transfer tokens: \"exactly `shares`\" cannot be honoured when the\n     *      transferred amount arrives short. Use `deposit` for those tokens.\n     */\n    function mint(uint256 shares, address receiver) public override nonReentrant returns (uint256 assets) {\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n\n        assets = previewMint(shares); // rounds up, in the vault's favour\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        (, uint256 received) = _pull(assets);\n        if (received != assets) revert InexactMint(assets, received);\n\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n        emit Deposit(msg.sender, receiver, assets, shares);\n    }","originalFile":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {ERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol\";\nimport {ERC4626} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/extensions/ERC4626.sol\";\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {SafeERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/utils/SafeERC20.sol\";\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\nimport {Math} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/math/Math.sol\";\n\nimport {TokenMetadata} from \"./libraries/TokenMetadata.sol\";\n\n/**\n * @title SaveVault\n * @notice A single-asset savings vault for one ERC-20. Depositors get a transferable ERC-4626\n *         receipt token representing a pro-rata claim on everything the vault holds.\n *\n * @dev Accounting model\n *      ------------------\n *      `totalAssets()` is the vault's live balance of the underlying, NOT an internal counter.\n *      That is what makes \"the keeper just sends tokens in\" work: a plain `transfer` into this\n *      contract raises `totalAssets()` without minting shares, so every share is instantly worth\n *      more. There is no `accrue()` to call, no reward index, and no per-user bookkeeping.\n *\n *      The flip side of balance-based accounting is that a *donation* is indistinguishable from\n *      yield, which is the classic ERC-4626 inflation attack. That is handled with a virtual\n *      share/asset offset of 1e6 (see `_decimalsOffset`), not by trying to detect donations.\n *\n * @dev Trust model\n *      -----------\n *      This vault is ownerless and immutable: no admin, no pause, no upgrade, no rescue function.\n *      Nobody — including the deployer — can freeze deposits, change the fee (there is none), or\n *      move user funds. The cost of that choice is that there is also no emergency stop if the\n *      *underlying* token turns out to be malicious. Listing a token is not an endorsement of it;\n *      the risk of the asset stays with the depositor. See NOTES.md.\n */\ncontract SaveVault is ERC4626, ReentrancyGuard {\n    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;\n    using Math for uint256;\n\n    /// @dev Virtual shares/assets exponent. Makes the first-depositor inflation attack cost\n    ///      ~1e6x the profit it could extract, which prices it out entirely.\n    uint8 private constant DECIMALS_OFFSET = 6;\n\n    /// @dev `decimals()` returns `assetDecimals + DECIMALS_OFFSET` as a uint8, so an absurd\n    ///      underlying would permanently revert it. Reject at construction instead.\n    uint8 internal constant MAX_ASSET_DECIMALS = 36;\n\n    /// @notice Factory that deployed this vault (address(0) if deployed standalone).\n    address public immutable factory;\n\n    /// @notice Emitted when yield is pushed in through `donate`. Plain transfers into the vault\n    ///         also count as yield but cannot emit an event — index `totalAssets()` for those.\n    event YieldAdded(address indexed from, uint256 amount, uint256 newTotalAssets);\n\n    error ZeroAmount();\n    error ZeroShares();\n    error ZeroAssets();\n    error ZeroAddress();\n    error UnsupportedDecimals(uint8 assetDecimals);\n    error InexactMint(uint256 requested, uint256 received);\n    error NoSharesOutstanding();\n\n    constructor(IERC20 asset_)\n        ERC20(TokenMetadata.vaultName(address(asset_)), TokenMetadata.vaultSymbol(address(asset_)))\n        ERC4626(asset_)\n    {\n        uint8 assetDecimals = TokenMetadata.safeDecimals(address(asset_));\n        if (assetDecimals > MAX_ASSET_DECIMALS) revert UnsupportedDecimals(assetDecimals);\n        factory = msg.sender;\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Deposits\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Deposit `assets` of the underlying and receive receipt shares.\n     * @dev Shares are minted against the amount the vault *actually received*, priced at the\n     *      share ratio from *before* the transfer. Both matter:\n     *      - fee-on-transfer tokens deliver less than `assets`; minting on the requested amount\n     *        would hand out unbacked shares and dilute existing holders;\n     *      - pricing after the transfer would let the depositor's own assets inflate the\n     *        denominator and shortchange them.\n     *      Consequence: for fee-on-transfer tokens the return value can be lower than\n     *      `previewDeposit(assets)`. That is a deliberate deviation from the ERC-4626 preview\n     *      guarantee; the alternative is silently socialising the fee onto existing depositors.\n     */\n    function deposit(uint256 assets, address receiver) public override nonReentrant returns (uint256 shares) {\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        (, shares) = _pullAndMint(assets, receiver);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Mint exactly `shares` receipt tokens, pulling however much underlying that costs.\n     * @dev Reverts for fee-on-transfer tokens: \"exactly `shares`\" cannot be honoured when the\n     *      transferred amount arrives short. Use `deposit` for those tokens.\n     */\n    function mint(uint256 shares, address receiver) public override nonReentrant returns (uint256 assets) {\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        assets = previewMint(shares); // rounds up, in the vault's favour\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        (uint256 received, uint256 mintedShares) = _pullAndMint(assets, receiver);\n        if (received != assets || mintedShares != shares) revert InexactMint(shares, mintedShares);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Withdrawals\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice Burn shares to withdraw exactly `assets` of the underlying.\n    /// @dev Fee-on-transfer tokens: the vault sends `assets`, `receiver` may net less.\n    function withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner)\n        public\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256 shares)\n    {\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n        shares = super.withdraw(assets, receiver, owner);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Burn exactly `shares` and withdraw the underlying they are worth.\n    function redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address owner)\n        public\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256 assets)\n    {\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n        assets = super.redeem(shares, receiver, owner);\n        // Dust redemptions that round to nothing would burn shares for free.\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAssets();\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Yield\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Push `amount` of the underlying in as yield, lifting every holder's claim.\n     * @dev Permissionless by design — the keeper needs no privileges, and anyone topping the\n     *      vault up only benefits existing holders. Functionally identical to transferring the\n     *      tokens in directly; this path just measures the real amount received and emits an\n     *      event, which is what the keeper should use so its deliveries are indexable.\n     */\n    function donate(uint256 amount) external nonReentrant {\n        if (amount == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        // With no shares outstanding there is nobody to credit, and the donation would instead\n        // wreck the share price for the next depositor.\n        if (totalSupply() == 0) revert NoSharesOutstanding();\n\n        IERC20 asset_ = IERC20(asset());\n        uint256 balanceBefore = asset_.balanceOf(address(this));\n        asset_.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\n        uint256 balanceAfter = asset_.balanceOf(address(this));\n\n        emit YieldAdded(msg.sender, balanceAfter - balanceBefore, balanceAfter);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Views\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /**\n     * @notice True while a deposit/withdraw is mid-flight inside this vault.\n     * @dev Integrators pricing this vault from inside an ERC-777/callback hook must check this.\n     *      During `deposit` the underlying has already landed but the shares are not minted yet,\n     *      so `convertToAssets` reads high for the duration of the callback. Read-only\n     *      reentrancy is not a reentrancy bug in this contract, it is a hazard for readers.\n     */\n    function isEntered() external view returns (bool) {\n        return _reentrancyGuardEntered();\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Internals\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function _decimalsOffset() internal pure override returns (uint8) {\n        return DECIMALS_OFFSET;\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Checks-effects-interactions cannot fully apply here: the amount received is only\n    ///      knowable after the transfer. `nonReentrant` on every entry point is what keeps the\n    ///      window safe, and the balance delta is read fresh rather than assumed.\n    function _pullAndMint(uint256 assets, address receiver) private returns (uint256 received, uint256 shares) {\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n\n        IERC20 asset_ = IERC20(asset());\n        uint256 totalAssetsBefore = asset_.balanceOf(address(this));\n        uint256 totalSupplyBefore = totalSupply();\n\n        asset_.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), assets);\n\n        // Reverts on underflow if the token somehow reduced our balance.\n        received = asset_.balanceOf(address(this)) - totalAssetsBefore;\n        if (received == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        // Same formula as ERC4626._convertToShares, evaluated at the pre-transfer state.\n        shares = received.mulDiv(totalSupplyBefore + 10 ** DECIMALS_OFFSET, totalAssetsBefore + 1, Math.Rounding.Floor);\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroShares();\n\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n        emit Deposit(msg.sender, receiver, received, shares);\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":88,"oldLines":7,"newStart":88,"newLines":18,"lines":["      */","     function deposit(uint256 Depositors get a transferable ERC-4626\n *         receipt token representing a pro-rata claim on everything the vault holds.\n *\n * @dev Accounting model\n *      ------------------\n *      `totalAssets()` is the vault's live balance of the underlying, NOT an internal counter.\n *      That is what makes \"the keeper just sends tokens in\" work: a plain `transfer` into this\n *      contract raises `totalAssets()` without minting shares, so every share is instantly worth\n *      more. There is no `accrue()` to call, no reward index, and no per-user bookkeeping.\n *\n *      The flip side of balance-based accounting is that a *donation* is indistinguishable from\n *      yield, which is the classic ERC-4626 inflation attack. That is handled with a virtual\n *      share/asset offset of 1e6 (see `_decimalsOffset`), not by trying to detect donations.\n *\n * @dev Trust model\n *      -----------\n *      This vault is ownerless and immutable: no admin, no pause, no upgrade, no rescue function.\n *      Nobody — including the deployer — can freeze deposits, change the fee (there is none), or\n *      move user funds. The cost of that choice is that there is also no emergency stop if the\n *      *underlying* token turns out to be malicious. Listing a token is not an endorsement of it;\n *      the risk of the asset stays with the depositor. See NOTES.md.\n */\ncontract SaveVault is ERC4626, ReentrancyGuard {\n    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;\n    using Math for uint256;\n\n    /// @dev Virtual shares/assets exponent. Makes the first-depositor inflation attack cost\n    ///      ~1e6x the profit it could extract, which prices it out entirely.\n    uint8 private constant DECIMALS_OFFSET = 6;\n\n    /// @dev `decimals()` returns `assetDecimals + DECIMALS_OFFSET` as a uint8, so an absurd\n    ///      underlying would permanently revert it. Reject at construction instead.\n    uint8 internal constant MAX_ASSET_DECIMALS = 36;\n\n    /// @notice Factory that deployed this vault (address(0) if deployed standalone).\n    address public immutable factory;\n\n    /// @notice Emitted when yield is pushed in through `donate`. Plain transfers into the vault\n    ///         also count as yield but cannot emit an event — index `totalAssets()` for those.\n    event YieldAdded(address indexed from, uint256 amount, uint256 newTotalAssets);\n\n    error ZeroAmount();\n    error ZeroShares();\n    error ZeroAssets();\n    error ZeroAddress();\n    error UnsupportedDecimals(uint8 assetDecimals);\n    error InexactMint(uint256 requested, uint256 received);\n    error NoSharesOutstanding();\n\n    constructor(IERC20 asset_)\n        ERC20(TokenMetadata.vaultName(address(asset_)), TokenMetadata.vaultSymbol(address(asset_)))\n        ERC4626(asset_)\n    {\n        uint8 assetDecimals = TokenMetadata.safeDecimals(address(asset_));\n        if (assetDecimals > MAX_ASSET_DECIMALS) revert UnsupportedDecimals(assetDecimals);\n        factory = msg.sender;\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Deposits\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Deposit `assets` of the underlying and receive receipt shares.\n     * @dev Shares are minted against the amount the vault *actually received*, priced at the\n     *      share ratio from *before* the transfer. Both matter:\n     *      - fee-on-transfer tokens deliver less than `assets`; minting on the requested amount\n     *        would hand out unbacked shares and dilute existing holders;\n     *      - pricing after the transfer would let the depositor's own assets inflate the\n     *        denominator and shortchange them.\n     *      Consequence: for fee-on-transfer tokens the return value can be lower than\n     *      `previewDeposit(assets)`. That is a deliberate deviation from the ERC-4626 preview\n     *      guarantee; the alternative is silently socialising the fee onto existing depositors.\n     */\n    function deposit(uint256 assets, address receiver) public override nonReentrant returns (uint256 shares) {\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n\n        uint256 totalSupplyBefore = totalSupply();\n        (uint256 totalAssetsBefore, uint256 received) = _pull(assets);\n        if (received == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        // Same formula as ERC4626._convertToShares, evaluated at the pre-transfer state.\n        shares = received.mulDiv(totalSupplyBefore + 10 ** DECIMALS_OFFSET, totalAssetsBefore + 1, Math.Rounding.Floor);\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroShares();\n\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n        emit Deposit(msg.sender, receiver, received, shares);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Mint exactly `shares` receipt tokens, pulling however much underlying that costs.\n     * @dev Reverts for fee-on-transfer tokens: \"exactly `shares`\" cannot be honoured when the\n     *      transferred amount arrives short. Use `deposit` for those tokens.\n     */\n    function mint(uint256 shares, address receiver) public override nonReentrant returns (uint256 assets) {\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n\n        assets = previewMint(shares); // rounds up, in the vault's favour\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        (, uint256 received) = _pull(assets);\n        if (received != assets) revert InexactMint(assets, received);\n\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n        emit Deposit(msg.sender, receiver, assets, shares);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Withdrawals\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice Burn shares to withdraw exactly `assets` of the underlying.\n    /// @dev Fee-on-transfer tokens: the vault sends `assets`, `receiver` may net less.\n    function withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner)\n        public\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256 shares)\n    {\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n        shares = super.withdraw(assets, receiver, owner);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Burn exactly `shares` and withdraw the underlying they are worth.\n    function redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address owner)\n        public\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256 assets)\n    {\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n        assets = super.redeem(shares, receiver, owner);\n        // Dust redemptions that round to nothing would burn shares for free.\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAssets();\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Yield\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Push `amount` of the underlying in as yield, lifting every holder's claim.\n     * @dev Permissionless by design — the keeper needs no privileges, and anyone topping the\n     *      vault up only benefits existing holders. Functionally identical to transferring the\n     *      tokens in directly; this path just measures the real amount received and emits an\n     *      event, which is what the keeper should use so its deliveries are indexable.\n     */\n    function donate(uint256 amount) external nonReentrant {\n        if (amount == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        // With no shares outstanding there is nobody to credit, and the donation would instead\n        // wreck the share price for the next depositor.\n        if (totalSupply() == 0) revert NoSharesOutstanding();\n\n        IERC20 asset_ = IERC20(asset());\n        uint256 balanceBefore = asset_.balanceOf(address(this));\n        asset_.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\n        uint256 balanceAfter = asset_.balanceOf(address(this));\n\n        emit YieldAdded(msg.sender, balanceAfter - balanceBefore, balanceAfter);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Views\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /**\n     * @notice True while a deposit/withdraw is mid-flight inside this vault.\n     * @dev Integrators pricing this vault from inside an ERC-777/callback hook must check this.\n     *      During `deposit` the underlying has already landed but the shares are not minted yet,\n     *      so `convertToAssets` reads high for the duration of the callback. Read-only\n     *      reentrancy is not a reentrancy bug in this contract, it is a hazard for readers.\n     */\n    function isEntered() external view returns (bool) {\n        return _reentrancyGuardEntered();\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Internals\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function _decimalsOffset() internal pure override returns (uint8) {\n        return DECIMALS_OFFSET;\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Checks-effects-interactions cannot fully apply here: the amount received is only\n    ///      knowable after the transfer. `nonReentrant` on every entry point is what keeps the\n    ///      window safe, and the balance delta is read fresh rather than assumed.\n    function _pullAndMint(uint256 assets, address receiver) private returns (uint256 received, uint256 shares) {\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n\n        IERC20 asset_ = IERC20(asset());\n        uint256 totalAssetsBefore = asset_.balanceOf(address(this));\n        uint256 totalSupplyBefore = totalSupply();\n\n        asset_.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), assets);\n\n        // Reverts on underflow if the token somehow reduced our balance.\n        received = asset_.balanceOf(address(this)) - totalAssetsBefore;\n        if (received == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        // Same formula as ERC4626._convertToShares, evaluated at the pre-transfer state.\n        shares = received.mulDiv(totalSupplyBefore + 10 ** DECIMALS_OFFSET, totalAssetsBefore + 1, Math.Rounding.Floor);\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroShares();\n\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n        emit Deposit(msg.sender, receiver, received, shares);\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":169,"oldLines":12,"newStart":169,"newLines":8,"lines":["         // wreck the share price for the next depositor.","         if (totalSupply() == 0) revert NoSharesOutstanding();"," ","-        IERC20 asset_ = IERC20(asset());","-        uint256 balanceBefore = asset_.balanceOf(address(this));","-        asset_.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);","-        uint256 balanceAfter = asset_.balanceOf(address(this));","-","-        emit YieldAdded(msg.sender, balanceAfter - totalAssetsBefore;\n    }","originalFile":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {ERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol\";\nimport {ERC4626} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/extensions/ERC4626.sol\";\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {SafeERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/utils/SafeERC20.sol\";\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\nimport {Math} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/math/Math.sol\";\n\nimport {TokenMetadata} from \"./libraries/TokenMetadata.sol\";\n\n/**\n * @title SaveVault\n * @notice A single-asset savings vault for one ERC-20. Depositors get a transferable ERC-4626\n *         receipt token representing a pro-rata claim on everything the vault holds.\n *\n * @dev Accounting model\n *      ------------------\n *      `totalAssets()` is the vault's live balance of the underlying, NOT an internal counter.\n *      That is what makes \"the keeper just sends tokens in\" work: a plain `transfer` into this\n *      contract raises `totalAssets()` without minting shares, so every share is instantly worth\n *      more. There is no `accrue()` to call, no reward index, and no per-user bookkeeping.\n *\n *      The flip side of balance-based accounting is that a *donation* is indistinguishable from\n *      yield, which is the classic ERC-4626 inflation attack. That is handled with a virtual\n *      share/asset offset of 1e6 (see `_decimalsOffset`), not by trying to detect donations.\n *\n * @dev Trust model\n *      -----------\n *      This vault is ownerless and immutable: no admin, no pause, no upgrade, no rescue function.\n *      Nobody — including the deployer — can freeze deposits, change the fee (there is none), or\n *      move user funds. The cost of that choice is that there is also no emergency stop if the\n *      *underlying* token turns out to be malicious. Listing a token is not an endorsement of it;\n *      the risk of the asset stays with the depositor. See NOTES.md.\n */\ncontract SaveVault is ERC4626, ReentrancyGuard {\n    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;\n    using Math for uint256;\n\n    /// @dev Virtual shares/assets exponent. Makes the first-depositor inflation attack cost\n    ///      ~1e6x the profit it could extract, which prices it out entirely.\n    uint8 private constant DECIMALS_OFFSET = 6;\n\n    /// @dev `decimals()` returns `assetDecimals + DECIMALS_OFFSET` as a uint8, so an absurd\n    ///      underlying would permanently revert it. Reject at construction instead.\n    uint8 internal constant MAX_ASSET_DECIMALS = 36;\n\n    /// @notice Factory that deployed this vault (address(0) if deployed standalone).\n    address public immutable factory;\n\n    /// @notice Emitted when yield is pushed in through `donate`. Plain transfers into the vault\n    ///         also count as yield but cannot emit an event — index `totalAssets()` for those.\n    event YieldAdded(address indexed from, uint256 amount, uint256 newTotalAssets);\n\n    error ZeroAmount();\n    error ZeroShares();\n    error ZeroAssets();\n    error ZeroAddress();\n    error UnsupportedDecimals(uint8 assetDecimals);\n    error InexactMint(uint256 requested, uint256 received);\n    error NoSharesOutstanding();\n\n    constructor(IERC20 asset_)\n        ERC20(TokenMetadata.vaultName(address(asset_)), TokenMetadata.vaultSymbol(address(asset_)))\n        ERC4626(asset_)\n    {\n        uint8 assetDecimals = TokenMetadata.safeDecimals(address(asset_));\n        if (assetDecimals > MAX_ASSET_DECIMALS) revert UnsupportedDecimals(assetDecimals);\n        factory = msg.sender;\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Deposits\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Deposit `assets` of the underlying and receive receipt shares.\n     * @dev Shares are minted against the amount the vault *actually received*, priced at the\n     *      share ratio from *before* the transfer. Both matter:\n     *      - fee-on-transfer tokens deliver less than `assets`; minting on the requested amount\n     *        would hand out unbacked shares and dilute existing holders;\n     *      - pricing after the transfer would let the depositor's own assets inflate the\n     *        denominator and shortchange them.\n     *      Consequence: for fee-on-transfer tokens the return value can be lower than\n     *      `previewDeposit(assets)`. That is a deliberate deviation from the ERC-4626 preview\n     *      guarantee; the alternative is silently socialising the fee onto existing depositors.\n     */\n    function deposit(uint256 assets, address receiver) public override nonReentrant returns (uint256 shares) {\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n\n        uint256 totalSupplyBefore = totalSupply();\n        (uint256 totalAssetsBefore, uint256 received) = _pull(assets);\n        if (received == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        // Same formula as ERC4626._convertToShares, evaluated at the pre-transfer state.\n        shares = received.mulDiv(totalSupplyBefore + 10 ** DECIMALS_OFFSET, totalAssetsBefore + 1, Math.Rounding.Floor);\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroShares();\n\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n        emit Deposit(msg.sender, receiver, received, shares);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Mint exactly `shares` receipt tokens, pulling however much underlying that costs.\n     * @dev Reverts for fee-on-transfer tokens: \"exactly `shares`\" cannot be honoured when the\n     *      transferred amount arrives short. Use `deposit` for those tokens.\n     */\n    function mint(uint256 shares, address receiver) public override nonReentrant returns (uint256 assets) {\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n\n        assets = previewMint(shares); // rounds up, in the vault's favour\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        (, uint256 received) = _pull(assets);\n        if (received != assets) revert InexactMint(assets, received);\n\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n        emit Deposit(msg.sender, receiver, assets, shares);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Withdrawals\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice Burn shares to withdraw exactly `assets` of the underlying.\n    /// @dev Fee-on-transfer tokens: the vault sends `assets`, `receiver` may net less.\n    function withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner)\n        public\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256 shares)\n    {\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n        shares = super.withdraw(assets, receiver, owner);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Burn exactly `shares` and withdraw the underlying they are worth.\n    function redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address owner)\n        public\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256 assets)\n    {\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n        assets = super.redeem(shares, receiver, owner);\n        // Dust redemptions that round to nothing would burn shares for free.\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAssets();\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Yield\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Push `amount` of the underlying in as yield, lifting every holder's claim.\n     * @dev Permissionless by design — the keeper needs no privileges, and anyone topping the\n     *      vault up only benefits existing holders. Functionally identical to transferring the\n     *      tokens in directly; this path just measures the real amount received and emits an\n     *      event, which is what the keeper should use so its deliveries are indexable.\n     */\n    function donate(uint256 amount) external nonReentrant {\n        if (amount == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        // With no shares outstanding there is nobody to credit, and the donation would instead\n        // wreck the share price for the next depositor.\n        if (totalSupply() == 0) revert NoSharesOutstanding();\n\n        (, uint256 received) = _pull(amount);\n        emit YieldAdded(msg.sender, received, totalAssets());\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Views\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /**\n     * @notice True while a deposit/withdraw is mid-flight inside this vault.\n     * @dev Integrators pricing this vault from inside an ERC-777/callback hook must check this.\n     *      During `deposit` the underlying has already landed but the shares are not minted yet,\n     *      so `convertToAssets` reads high for the duration of the callback.
