Its only jobs are (a) making sure there is\n *      one canonical vault per token so liquidity and receipt tokens do not fragment across\n *      duplicates, and (b) giving frontends a deterministic address to look up.\n *\n *      Listing is NOT curation. The checks below only reject inputs that would produce a vault\n *      that cannot work at all (an EOA, a contract with no `balanceOf`). They say nothing about\n *      whether the token is safe to hold — see NOTES.md for what an operator must vet.\n */\ncontract SaveVaultFactory {\n    /// @notice token => its canonical vault (address(0) if not listed).\n    mapping(address token => address vault) public vaultFor;\n\n    /// @notice Every vault ever created, in listing order.\n    address[] public allVaults;\n\n    /// @dev Precomputed so `predictVault` stays cheap.\n    bytes32 public immutable vaultInitCodeHash;\n\n    event VaultCreated(address indexed token, address indexed vault, address indexed creator, uint256 index);\n\n    error ZeroAddress();\n    error NotAContract(address token);\n    error NotAnERC20(address token);\n    error VaultAlreadyExists(address token, address vault);\n\n    constructor() {\n        vaultInitCodeHash = keccak256(type(SaveVault).creationCode);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Deploy the canonical vault for `token`.\n     * @dev CREATE2 with the token address as salt, so the vault address is knowable before it\n     *      exists and a second deployment for the same token is impossible even if the registry\n     *      mapping were somehow bypassed.\n     */\n    function createVault(address token) external returns (address vault) {\n        if (token == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n\n        // A vault over an EOA (or a not-yet-deployed address) would accept nothing and could\n        // later be backed by whatever code lands there.\n        if (token.code.length == 0) revert NotAContract(token);\n\n        // Cheapest honest liveness probe: the vault's entire accounting reads `balanceOf`.\n        // A contract that cannot answer it is not a token we can hold.\n        (bool ok, bytes memory ret) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeCall(IERC20.balanceOf, (address(this))));\n        if (!ok || ret.length < 32) revert NotAnERC20(token);\n\n        address existing = vaultFor[token];\n        if (existing != address(0)) revert VaultAlreadyExists(token, existing);\n\n        vault = address(new SaveVault{salt: bytes32(uint256(uint160(token)))}(IERC20(token)));\n\n        vaultFor[token] = vault;\n        allVaults.push(vault);\n\n        emit VaultCreated(token, vault, msg.sender, allVaults.length - 1);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Address `token`'s vault has, or would have, regardless of whether it is deployed.\n    function predictVault(address token) external view returns (address) {\n        return address(\n            uint160(\n                uint256(\n                    keccak256(\n                        abi.encodePacked(\n                            bytes1(0xff), address(this), bytes32(uint256(uint160(token))), vaultInitCodeHash\n                        )\n                    )\n                )\n            )\n        );\n    }\n\n    function vaultCount() external view returns (uint256) {\n        return allVaults.length;\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1210,"cache_read_input_tokens":67810,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1210},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"78210e2d-ae8e-4bb2-a869-e8efb63e9f6d","uuid":"d7922fc5-bc97-485e-9785-8cbed87eed75","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:34:24.455Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTp5ZTbjdnTJ1c5kvLD"}

\"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\n\nimport {SaveVault} from \"./SaveVault.sol\";\n\n/**\n * @title SaveVaultFactory\n * @notice Permissionless registry + deployer: anyone can list any ERC-20, exactly once.\n *\n * @dev The factory is ownerless and holds no funds. Its only jobs are (a) making sure there is\n *      one canonical vault per token so liquidity and receipt tokens do not fragment across\n *      duplicates, and (b) giving frontends a deterministic address to look up.\n *\n *      Listing is NOT curation. The checks below only reject inputs that would produce a vault\n *      that cannot work at all (an EOA, a contract with no `balanceOf`). They say nothing about\n *      whether the token is safe to hold — see NOTES.md for what an operator must vet.\n */\ncontract SaveVaultFactory {\n    /// @notice token => its canonical vault (address(0) if not listed).\n    mapping(address token => address vault) public vaultFor;\n\n    /// @notice Every vault ever created, in listing order.\n    address[] public allVaults;\n\n    event VaultCreated(address indexed token, address indexed vault, address indexed creator, uint256 index);\n\n    error ZeroAddress();\n    error NotAContract(address token);\n    error NotAnERC20(address token);\n    error VaultAlreadyExists(address token, address vault);\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Deploy the canonical vault for `token`.\n     * @dev CREATE2 with the token address as salt, so the vault address is knowable before it\n     *      exists and a second deployment for the same token is impossible even if the registry\n     *      mapping were somehow bypassed.\n     */\n    function createVault(address token) external returns (address vault) {\n        if (token == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n\n        // A vault over an EOA (or a not-yet-deployed address) would accept nothing and could\n        // later be backed by whatever code lands there.\n        if (token.code.length == 0) revert NotAContract(token);\n\n        // Cheapest honest liveness probe: the vault's entire accounting reads `balanceOf`.\n        // A contract that cannot answer it is not a token we can hold.\n        (bool ok, bytes memory ret) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeCall(IERC20.balanceOf, (address(this))));\n        if (!ok || ret.length < 32) revert NotAnERC20(token);\n\n        address existing = vaultFor[token];\n        if (existing != address(0)) revert VaultAlreadyExists(token, existing);\n\n        vault = address(new SaveVault{salt: bytes32(uint256(uint160(token)))}(IERC20(token)));\n\n        vaultFor[token] = vault;\n        allVaults.push(vault);\n\n        emit VaultCreated(token, vault, msg.sender, allVaults.length - 1);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Address `token`'s vault has, or would have, regardless of whether it is deployed.\n    function Real symbols are <= ~11 chars.\n    uint256 private constant MAX_SYMBOL_BYTES = 32;\n\n    /// @dev Matches OpenZeppelin's ERC4626 fallback when `decimals()` is unreadable.\n    uint8 internal constant DEFAULT_DECIMALS = 18;\n\n    /// @notice Name for the receipt token of a vault holding `token`.\n    function vaultName(address token) internal view returns (string memory) {\n        return string.concat(\"Saved \", _symbolOr(token, \"Token\"));\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Symbol for the receipt token of a vault holding `token`.\n    /// @dev Not unique: two different tokens may report the same symbol. Index by vault address.\n    function vaultSymbol(address token) internal view returns (string memory) {\n        return string.concat(\"sv\", _symbolOr(token, \"TKN\"));\n    }\n\n    /// @notice `token.decimals()`, or `DEFAULT_DECIMALS` if the call fails or is malformed.\n    function safeDecimals(address token) internal view returns (uint8) {\n        (bool ok, bytes memory ret) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSignature(\"decimals()\"));\n        if (!ok || ret.length != 32) return DEFAULT_DECIMALS;\n        uint256 value = abi.decode(ret, (uint256));\n        if (value > type(uint8).max) return DEFAULT_DECIMALS;\n        return uint8(value);\n    }\n\n    function _symbolOr(address token, string memory fallbackSymbol) private view returns (string memory) {\n        string memory symbol_ = _readString(token, abi.encodeWithSignature(\"symbol()\"));\n        return bytes(symbol_).length == 0 ? fallbackSymbol : symbol_;\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Returns \"\" for any return shape we do not fully understand.\n    function _readString(address token, bytes memory callData) private view returns (string memory) {\n        (bool ok, bytes memory ret) = token.staticcall(callData);\n        if (!ok) return \"\";\n\n        if (ret.length == 32) {\n            // bytes32-style metadata (MKR and other pre-standard tokens).\n            return _sanitize(_unpackBytes32(abi.decode(ret, (bytes32))));\n        }\n\n        // ABI-encoded string: [offset][length][data...]. Reject anything not in canonical form.\n        if (ret.length < 64) return \"\";\n        uint256 offset = _word(ret, 0);\n        if (offset != 32) return \"\";\n        uint256 length = _word(ret, 32);\n        if (length == 0 || 64 + length > ret.length) return \"\";\n        if (length > MAX_SYMBOL_BYTES) length = MAX_SYMBOL_BYTES;\n\n        bytes memory raw = new bytes(length);\n        for (uint256 i; {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTuo99vmY4h9tagwU7k","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_013pLmUNnYekHa87DJSW2tDA","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122528Z-claude-with-skill-2/workspace/test/SaveVault.t.sol","content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {Test} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\n\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {IERC20Metadata} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/extensions/IERC20Metadata.sol\";\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\n\nimport {SaveVault} from \"../src/SaveVault.sol\";\nimport {SaveVaultFactory} from \"../src/SaveVaultFactory.sol\";\nimport {\n    Bytes32MetadataToken,\n    FeeOnTransferERC20,\n    HostileSymbolToken,\n    MockERC20,\n    NoMetadataNoReturnToken,\n    NotAToken,\n    ReentrantERC20\n} from \"./mocks/Tokens.sol\";\n\ncontract SaveVaultTest is Test {\n    SaveVaultFactory factory;\n    MockERC20 usdc; // 6 decimals, the decimals trap\n    SaveVault vault;\n\n    address alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n    address keeper = makeAddr(\"keeper\");\n    address attacker = makeAddr(\"attacker\");\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        factory = new SaveVaultFactory();\n        usdc = new MockERC20(\"USD Coin\", \"USDC\", 6);\n        vault = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(usdc)));\n\n        for (uint256 i; i < 4; ++i) {\n            address who = [alice, bob, keeper, attacker][i];\n            usdc.mint(who, 1_000_000e6);\n            vm.prank(who);\n            usdc.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Factory\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_factory_deploysAtPredictedAddress() public view {\n        assertEq(factory.vaultFor(address(usdc)), address(vault));\n        assertEq(factory.predictVault(address(usdc)), address(vault));\n        assertEq(factory.vaultCount(), 1);\n        assertEq(vault.asset(), address(usdc));\n        assertEq(vault.factory(), address(factory));\n    }\n\n    function test_factory_rejectsDuplicateListing() public {\n        vm.expectRevert(\n            abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.VaultAlreadyExists.selector, address(usdc), address(vault))\n        );\n        factory.createVault(address(usdc));\n    }\n\n    function test_factory_rejectsZeroAndEoaAndNonToken() public {\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVaultFactory.ZeroAddress.selector);\n        factory.createVault(address(0));\n\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.NotAContract.selector, alice));\n        factory.createVault(alice);\n\n        address notAToken = address(new NotAToken());\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.NotAnERC20.selector, notAToken));\n        factory.createVault(notAToken);\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Receipt token metadata\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_metadata_followsUnderlyingDecimals() public view {\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(vault)).name(), \"Saved USDC\");\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(vault)).symbol(), \"svUSDC\");\n        // 6 (underlying) + 6 (virtual offset)\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(vault)).decimals(), 12);\n    }\n\n    function test_metadata_handlesBytes32Symbol() public {\n        Bytes32MetadataToken mkr = new Bytes32MetadataToken();\n        SaveVault v = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(mkr)));\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(v)).symbol(), \"svMKR\");\n    }\n\n    function test_metadata_handlesMissingMetadata() public {\n        NoMetadataNoReturnToken weird = new NoMetadataNoReturnToken();\n        SaveVault v = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(weird)));\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(v)).symbol(), \"svTKN\");\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(v)).name(), \"Saved Token\");\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(v)).decimals(), 24); // 18 fallback + 6\n    }\n\n    function test_metadata_sanitisesHostileSymbol() public {\n        HostileSymbolToken hostile = new HostileSymbolToken();\n        SaveVault v = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(hostile)));\n        string memory symbol_ = IERC20Metadata(address(v)).symbol();\n        // Control bytes dropped, length capped: \"sv\" + 32 sanitised bytes at most.\n        assertLe(bytes(symbol_).length, 34);\n        for (uint256 i; i < bytes(symbol_).length; ++i) {\n            uint8 c = uint8(bytes(symbol_)[i]);\n            assertTrue(c >= 0x20 && c <= 0x7E, \"non-printable byte leaked into symbol\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Core claim math\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_deposit_thenRedeemRoundTrip() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), shares);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1_000e6);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 assets = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n\n        assertEq(assets, 1_000e6);\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), 0);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 0);\n    }\n\n    /// Yield is a plain transfer from the keeper. No accrue call, no index update.\n    function test_keeperTransferLiftsEveryClaimProRata() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.deposit(3_000e6, bob);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 400e6); // 10% yield on 4,000\n\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 1_100e6, 1);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 3_300e6, 1);\n    }\n\n    /// A depositor who arrives after the yield does not retroactively share in it.\n    function test_lateDepositorDoesNotDiluteEarlierYield() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 1_000e6); // alice's claim doubles\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.deposit(2_000e6, bob);\n\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 2_000e6, 1);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 2_000e6, 1);\n    }\n\n    function test_donateEmitsAndCreditsHolders() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n\n        vm.expectEmit(true, false, false, true, address(vault));\n        emit SaveVault.YieldAdded(keeper, 100e6, 1_100e6);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        vault.donate(100e6);\n\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 1_100e6, 1);\n    }\n\n    function test_donateRevertsWithNoHolders() public {\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.NoSharesOutstanding.selector);\n        vault.donate(100e6);\n    }\n\n    /// Receipt tokens are transferable and carry the claim with them.\n    function test_sharesAreTransferableClaims() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.transfer(bob, shares);\n\n SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(usdc)));\n\n        for (uint256 i; i < 4; ++i) {\n            address who = [alice, bob, keeper, attacker][i];\n            usdc.mint(who, 1_000_000e6);\n assertEq(vault.factory(), address(factory));\n    }\n\n    function test_factory_rejectsDuplicateListing() public {\n        vm.expectRevert(\n            abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.VaultAlreadyExists.selector, address(usdc), address(vault))\n        );\n        factory.createVault(address(usdc));\n    }\n\n    function test_factory_rejectsZeroAndEoaAndNonToken() public {\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVaultFactory.ZeroAddress.selector);\n        factory.createVault(address(0));\n\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.NotAContract.selector, alice));\n        factory.createVault(alice);\n\n        address notAToken = address(new NotAToken());\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.NotAnERC20.selector, notAToken));\n        factory.createVault(notAToken);\n    }\n\n    // test_metadata_followsUnderlyingDecimals() public view {\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(vault)).name(), \"Saved USDC\");\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(vault)).symbol(), \"svUSDC\");\n        // 6 (underlying) + 6 (virtual offset)\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(vault)).decimals(), 12);\n    }\n\n    function test_metadata_handlesBytes32Symbol() public {\n        Bytes32MetadataToken mkr = new Bytes32MetadataToken();\n        SaveVault v = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(mkr)));\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(v)).symbol(), \"svMKR\");\n    }\n\n    function test_metadata_handlesMissingMetadata() public {\n        NoMetadataNoReturnToken weird = new NoMetadataNoReturnToken();\n        SaveVault v = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(weird)));\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(v)).symbol(), \"svTKN\");\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(v)).name(), \"Saved Token\");\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(v)).decimals(), 24); // 18 fallback + 6\n    }\n\n    function test_metadata_sanitisesHostileSymbol() public {\n        HostileSymbolToken hostile = new HostileSymbolToken();\n        SaveVault v = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(hostile)));\n        string memory symbol_ = IERC20Metadata(address(v)).symbol();\n        // Control bytes dropped, length capped: \"sv\" + 32 sanitised bytes at most.\n        assertLe(bytes(symbol_).length, 34);\n        for (uint256 i; i < bytes(symbol_).length; ++i) {\n            uint8 c = uint8(bytes(symbol_)[i]);\n            assertTrue(c >= 0x20 && c <= 0x7E, \"non-printable byte leaked into symbol\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    // test_deposit_thenRedeemRoundTrip() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), shares);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1_000e6);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 assets = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n\n        assertEq(assets, 1_000e6);\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), 0);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 0);\n    }\n\n    /// Yield is a plain transfer from the keeper. test_lateDepositorDoesNotDiluteEarlierYield() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 1_000e6); }\n\n    function test_zeroReceiverReverts() public {\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAddress.selector);\n        vault.deposit(1e6, address(0));\n\n        vault.deposit(1e6, alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAddress.selector);\n        vault.withdraw(1, address(0), alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function test_cannotWithdrawSomeoneElsesShares() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        vault.redeem(shares, bob, alice);\n    }\n\n    /// Third-party tokens sent here by mistake are unrecoverable — there is no rescue hook,\n    /// and by design nothing can move the underlying except share redemption.\n    function test_noRescueFunctionExists() public {\n        MockERC20 stray = new MockERC20(\"Stray\", \"STR\", 18);\n        stray.mint(address(vault), 1e18);\n        assertEq(stray.balanceOf(address(vault)), 1e18);\n        // Nothing in the ABI can move it; asserted by the absence of any owner/admin entry point.\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 0, \"stray token must not count as underlying\");\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Fuzz\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// A depositor can never redeem more than they put in when no yield arrived.\n    function testFuzz_noValueCreatedOnRoundTrip(uint256 seed, uint128 aliceIn, uint128 bobIn) public {\n        aliceIn = uint128(bound(aliceIn, 1e6, 1_000_000e6));\n        bobIn = uint128(bound(bobIn, 1e6, 1_000_000e6));\n        uint256 yield_ = bound(seed, 0, 1_000_000e6);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 aliceShares = vault.deposit(aliceIn, alice);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 bobShares = vault.deposit(bobIn, bob);\n\n        if (yield_ > 0) {\n            vm.prank(keeper);\n            usdc.transfer(address(vault), yield_);\n        }\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 aliceOut = vault.redeem(aliceShares, alice, alice);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 bobOut = vault.redeem(bobShares, bob, bob);\n\n        // Nobody can extract more than the vault ever held.\n        assertLe(aliceOut + bobOut, uint256(aliceIn) + bobIn + yield_);\n        // Each depositor gets back at least their principal minus rounding dust.\n        assertGe(aliceOut + 1, aliceIn);\n        assertGe(bobOut + 1, bobIn);\n    }\n\n    function testFuzz_donationCannotStealFromExistingHolder(uint128 depositIn, uint128 donation) public {\n        depositIn = uint128(bound(depositIn, 1e6, 1_000_000e6));\n        donation = uint128(bound(donation, 0, 1_000_000e6));\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 aliceShares = vault.deposit(depositIn, alice);\n\n        if (donation > 0) {\n            vm.prank(attacker);\n            usdc.transfer(address(vault), donation);\n        }\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 aliceOut = vault.redeem(aliceShares, alice, alice);\n        assertGe(aliceOut + 1, depositIn);\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}

SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {Test} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\n\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {IERC20Metadata} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/extensions/IERC20Metadata.sol\";\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\n\nimport {SaveVault} from \"../src/SaveVault.sol\";\nimport {SaveVaultFactory} from \"../src/SaveVaultFactory.sol\";\nimport {\n    Bytes32MetadataToken,\n    FeeOnTransferERC20,\n    HostileSymbolToken,\n    MockERC20,\n    NoMetadataNoReturnToken,\n    NotAToken,\n    ReentrantERC20\n} from \"./mocks/Tokens.sol\";\n\ncontract SaveVaultTest is Test {\n    SaveVaultFactory factory;\n    MockERC20 usdc; // 6 decimals, the decimals trap\n    SaveVault vault;\n\n    address alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n    address keeper = makeAddr(\"keeper\");\n    address attacker = makeAddr(\"attacker\");\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        factory = new SaveVaultFactory();\n        usdc = new MockERC20(\"USD Coin\", \"USDC\", 6);\n        vault = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(usdc)));\n\n        for (uint256 i; i < 4; ++i) {\n            address who = [alice, bob, keeper, attacker][i];\n            usdc.mint(who, 1_000_000e6);\n            vm.prank(who);\n            usdc.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Factory\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_factory_deploysAtPredictedAddress() public view {\n        assertEq(factory.vaultFor(address(usdc)), address(vault));\n        assertEq(factory.predictVault(address(usdc)), address(vault));\n        assertEq(factory.vaultCount(), 1);\n        assertEq(vault.asset(), address(usdc));\n        assertEq(vault.factory(), address(factory));\n    }\n\n    function test_factory_rejectsDuplicateListing() public {\n        vm.expectRevert(\n            abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.VaultAlreadyExists.selector, address(usdc), address(vault))\n        );\n        factory.createVault(address(usdc));\n    }\n\n    function test_factory_rejectsZeroAndEoaAndNonToken() public {\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVaultFactory.ZeroAddress.selector);\n        factory.createVault(address(0));\n\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.NotAContract.selector, alice));\n        factory.createVault(alice);\n\n        address notAToken = address(new NotAToken());\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.NotAnERC20.selector, notAToken));\n        factory.createVault(notAToken);\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Receipt token metadata\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_metadata_followsUnderlyingDecimals() public view {\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(vault)).name(), \"Saved USDC\");\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(vault)).symbol(), \"svUSDC\");\n        // 6 (underlying) + 6 (virtual offset)\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(vault)).decimals(), 12);\n    }\n\n    function test_metadata_handlesBytes32Symbol() public {\n        Bytes32MetadataToken mkr = new Bytes32MetadataToken();\n        SaveVault v = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(mkr)));\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(v)).symbol(), \"svMKR\");\n    }\n\n    function test_metadata_handlesMissingMetadata() public {\n        NoMetadataNoReturnToken weird = new NoMetadataNoReturnToken();\n        SaveVault v = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(weird)));\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(v)).symbol(), \"svTKN\");\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(v)).name(), \"Saved Token\");\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(v)).decimals(), 24); // 18 fallback + 6\n    }\n\n    function test_metadata_sanitisesHostileSymbol() public {\n        HostileSymbolToken hostile = new HostileSymbolToken();\n        SaveVault v = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(hostile)));\n        string memory symbol_ = IERC20Metadata(address(v)).symbol();\n        // Control bytes dropped, assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 2_000e6, 1);\n    }\n\n    function test_donateEmitsAndCreditsHolders() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n\n        vm.expectEmit(true, false, false, true, address(vault));\n        emit SaveVault.YieldAdded(keeper, 100e6, 1_100e6);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        vault.donate(100e6);\n\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 1_100e6, 1);\n    }\n\n    function test_donateRevertsWithNoHolders() public {\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.NoSharesOutstanding.selector);\n        vault.donate(100e6);\n    }\n\n    /// Receipt tokens are transferable and carry the claim with them.\n    function test_sharesAreTransferableClaims() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.transfer(bob, shares);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100e6);\n\n        assertEq(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 0);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 1_100e6, 1);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.redeem(shares, bob, bob);\n        // bob's own 1,000,000 float + alice's 1,000 principal + the 100 of yield\n        assertApproxEqAbs(usdc.balanceOf(bob), 1_001_100e6, 1);\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Inflation / donation attack\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// The classic first-depositor attack: 1 wei deposit, then a fat donation to inflate the\n    /// share price so the victim's deposit rounds to zero shares.\n    function test_inflationAttackIsNotProfitable() public {\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        uint256 attackerShares = vault.deposit(1, attacker);\n\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100_000e6); // donation, not a deposit\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 victimShares = vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n        assertGt(victimShares, 0, \"victim rounded to zero shares\");\n\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        uint256 attackerOut = vault.redeem(attackerShares, attacker, attacker);\n\n        uint256 attackerSpent = 100_000e6 + 1;\n        assertLt(attackerOut, attackerSpent, \"attack turned a profit\");\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 victimOut = vault.redeem(victimShares, alice, alice);\n        // Victim loses at most rounding dust, not a slice of their principal.\n        assertApproxEqRel(victimOut, 1_000e6, 1e12); // within 0.0001%\n    }\n\n    function test_dustDepositRevertsRatherThanMintingZeroShares() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 1e30); // absurd share price\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroShares.selector);\n        vault.deposit(1, bob);\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Hostile token behaviour\n SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(fee)));\n\n        fee.mint(alice, 1_000e18);\n        fee.mint(bob, 1_000e18);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        fee.approve(address(v), type(uint256).max);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        fee.approve(address(v), type(uint256).max);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        v.deposit(1_000e18, alice);\n        uint256 aliceClaimBefore = v.maxWithdraw(alice);\n\n        fee.setFeeBps(1_000); // 10% fee switched on afterwards, as real tokens do\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 bobShares = v.deposit(1_000e18, bob);\n\n        assertGe(v.maxWithdraw(alice), aliceClaimBefore, \"existing holder diluted by the fee\");\n        // Bob is credited for the 900 that landed, not the 1,000 he sent.\n }\n\n    function test_reentrantDepositIsBlocked() public {\n        ReentrantERC20 hook = new ReentrantERC20();\n        SaveVault v = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(hook)));\n\n attacker)));\n\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        vm.expectRevert(ReentrancyGuard.ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall.selector);\n        v.deposit(10e18, attacker);\n    }\n\n    function test_reentrantRedeemIsBlocked() public {\n        ReentrantERC20 hook = new ReentrantERC20();\n        SaveVault v = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(hook)));\n\n        hook.mint(attacker, 1_000e18);\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        hook.approve(address(v), type(uint256).max);\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        uint256 shares = v.deposit(10e18, attacker);\n\n        hook.arm(address(v), abi.encodeCall(SaveVault.redeem, (shares / 2, attacker, attacker)));\n\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        vm.expectRevert(ReentrancyGuard.ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall.selector);\n        v.redeem(shares, attacker, attacker);\n    }\n\n    /// USDT-style: no boolean return value. SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(usdt)));\n\n        usdt.mint(alice, 1_000e18);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        usdt.approve(address(v), type(uint256).max);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n test_zeroValueCallsRevert() public {\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAmount.selector);\n        vault.deposit(0, alice);\n vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAmount.selector);\n        vault.redeem(0, alice, alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAmount.selector);\n        vault.donate(0);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n Both matter:\n81\t     *      - fee-on-transfer tokens deliver less than `assets`; minting on the requested amount\n82\t     *        would hand out unbacked shares and dilute existing holders;\n83\t     *      - pricing after the transfer would let the depositor's own assets inflate the\n84\t     *        denominator and shortchange them.\n85\t     *      Consequence: for fee-on-transfer tokens the return value can be lower than\n86\t     *      `previewDeposit(assets)`. That is a deliberate deviation from the ERC-4626 preview\n87\t     *      guarantee; the alternative is silently socialising the fee onto existing depositors.\n88\t     */\n89\t    function deposit(uint256 assets, address receiver) public override nonReentrant returns (uint256 shares) {\n90\t        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n91\t        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n92\t\n93\t        uint256 totalSupplyBefore = totalSupply();\n94\t        (uint256 totalAssetsBefore, uint256 received) = _pull(assets);\n95\t        if (received == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n96\t\n97\t        // Same formula as ERC4626._convertToShares, evaluated at the pre-transfer state.\n98\t        shares = received.mulDiv(totalSupplyBefore + 10 ** DECIMALS_OFFSET, totalAssetsBefore + 1, Math.Rounding.Floor);\n99\t        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroShares();\n100\t\n101\t        _mint(receiver, shares);\n102\t        emit Deposit(msg.sender, receiver, received, shares);\n103\t    }\n104\t\n105\t    /**\n106\t     * @notice Mint exactly `shares` receipt tokens, pulling however much underlying that costs.\n107\t     * @dev Reverts for fee-on-transfer tokens: \"exactly `shares`\" cannot be honoured when the\n108\t     *      transferred amount arrives short. Both matter:\n     *      - fee-on-transfer tokens deliver less than `assets`; minting on the requested amount\n     *        would hand out unbacked shares and dilute existing holders;\n     *      - pricing after the transfer would let the depositor's own assets inflate the\n     *        denominator and shortchange them.\n     *      Consequence: for fee-on-transfer tokens the return value can be lower than\n     *      `previewDeposit(assets)`. That is a deliberate deviation from the ERC-4626 preview\n     *      guarantee; the alternative is silently socialising the fee onto existing depositors.\n     */\n    function deposit(uint256 assets, address receiver) public override nonReentrant returns (uint256 shares) {\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n\n        uint256 totalSupplyBefore = totalSupply();\n        (uint256 totalAssetsBefore, uint256 received) = _pull(assets);\n        if (received == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        // Same formula as ERC4626._convertToShares, evaluated at the pre-transfer state.\n        shares = received.mulDiv(totalSupplyBefore + 10 ** DECIMALS_OFFSET, totalAssetsBefore + 1, Math.Rounding.Floor);\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroShares();\n\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n        emit Deposit(msg.sender, receiver, received, shares);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Mint exactly `shares` receipt tokens, pulling however much underlying that costs.\n     * @dev Reverts for fee-on-transfer tokens: \"exactly `shares`\" cannot be honoured when the\n     *      transferred amount arrives short. Use `deposit` for those tokens.\n     */\n    function mint(uint256 shares, address receiver) public override nonReentrant returns (uint256 assets) {\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n\n        assets = previewMint(shares); // rounds up, in the vault's favour\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        (, uint256 received) = _pull(assets);\n        if (received != assets) revert InexactMint(assets, received);\n\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n        emit Deposit(msg.sender, receiver, assets, shares);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Withdrawals\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice Burn shares to withdraw exactly `assets` of the underlying.\n    /// @dev Fee-on-transfer tokens: the vault sends `assets`, `receiver` may net less.\n    function withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner)\n        public\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256 shares)","numLines":60,"startLine":75,"totalLines":215}}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUU61Rcmd93T2CToqqfE","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01UTys9LPUw2Bnnk9EtvWmxw","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122528Z-claude-with-skill-2/workspace/NOTES.md","content":"# NOTES\n\nOnchain piece of \"save any token\". Two contracts:\n\n- `src/SaveVaultFactory.sol` — permissionless registry. Anyone lists any ERC-20, once.\n- `src/SaveVault.sol` — one vault per token. ERC-4626. The receipt token *is* the vault.\n\nDeploy the factory (`script/DeployFactory.s.sol`); everything else happens permissionlessly.\n\n```\nforge build\nforge test\n```\n\n---\n\n## How a depositor's claim is computed\n\n**One sentence:** your shares are a fixed slice of the vault's live token balance, and the keeper\nsending tokens in makes every slice worth more without changing anyone's share count.\n\n### The formula\n\n`totalAssets()` is **the vault's actual ERC-20 balance**, not an internal counter:\n\n```solidity\nfunction totalAssets() public view returns (uint256) {\n    return IERC20(asset()).balanceOf(address(this));\n}\n```\n\nEverything follows from that. Deposits price at the ratio *before* the incoming transfer:\n\n```\nshares  = assetsReceived * (totalSupply + 1e6) / (totalAssetsBefore + 1)     // rounds down\nassets  = shares         * (totalAssets + 1)  / (totalSupply  + 1e6)         // rounds down\n```\n\nThe `+ 1e6` and `+ 1` are **virtual shares and a virtual asset** (`_decimalsOffset() = 6`).\nSee \"Inflation attack\" below — they are load-bearing, not cosmetic.\n\nRounding always favours the vault (i.e. the other depositors), never the caller: shares out round\ndown, shares burned on `withdraw` round up. A depositor can lose at most 1 wei to rounding on a\nround trip, and can never mint value out of thin air. Both properties are fuzzed in\n`testFuzz_noValueCreatedOnRoundTrip`.\n\n### Why yield needs no accounting at all\n\nThe keeper's `transfer` raises `balanceOf(vault)` and therefore `totalAssets()`. `totalSupply()`\ndoes not move. So the claim behind every share rises simultaneously and proportionally. There is\nno reward index, no `accrue()`, no per-user checkpoint, and nothing to migrate when a holder\ntransfers their receipt token — the claim travels with the token because the claim *is* the token.\n\nWorked example (USDC, 6 decimals):\n\n| step                          | totalAssets | totalSupply | alice's claim | bob's claim |\n| ----------------------------- | ----------- | ----------- | ------------- | ----------- |\n| alice deposits 1,000          | 1,000       | 1.0e9 sv    | 1,000         | –           |\n| bob deposits 3,000            | 4,000       | 4.0e9 sv    | 1,000         | 3,000       |\n| keeper transfers in 400       | 4,400       | 4.0e9 sv    | **1,100**     | **3,300**   |\n| bob redeems everything        | 1,100       | 1.0e9 sv    | 1,100         | –           |\n\nYield accrues **only to holders at the time it lands**. A depositor arriving after the transfer\nbuys in at the new, higher price and gets no retroactive share of it\n(`test_lateDepositorDoesNotDiluteEarlierYield`).\n\n### Receipt token shape\n\n`decimals() = underlying.decimals() + 6`. A USDC vault issues 12-decimal `svUSDC`; a DAI vault\nissues 24-decimal `svDAI`. **Do not assume 18, and do not assume it matches the underlying** — the\n`+6` is the virtual-share offset. Name/symbol are derived from the underlying and are *not unique*\n(two tokens can both claim `USDC`). Index vaults by address, never by symbol.\n\n---\n\n## What the operator has to get right\n\n### Listing a token\n\nThe factory's checks are deliberately minimal — reject only what cannot possibly work:\n\n- `token != address(0)`\n- `token.code.length > 0` (no vault over an EOA, or over an address where code might land later)\n- `token.balanceOf(...)` answers (the whole accounting model reads it)\n- no existing vault for that token — CREATE2 with the token as salt makes duplicates impossible\n  even if the registry mapping were bypassed\n\n**Listing is not curation.** Passing those checks says nothing about whether the token is safe to\nhold. The things that will actually bite, in rough order of likelihood:\n\n- **Fee-on-transfer.** Handled: `deposit` mints against the balance delta, so an incoming fee is\n  paid by the depositor, not socialised onto everyone already in the vault\n  (`test_feeOnTransferDepositDoesNotDiluteExistingHolders`). Two consequences to surface in the UI:\n  `previewDeposit` overstates the shares you will get, and `mint` reverts with `InexactMint`\n  (it cannot honour \"exactly N shares\"). Route those tokens through `deposit`. Note many tokens\n  ship with the fee at 0 and a switch to turn it on later — do not decide this at listing time.\n- **Rebasing / balance-changing tokens (stETH, AMPL).** A positive rebase is treated exactly like\n  yield, which is fine. A **negative** rebase silently reduces everyone's claim pro-rata with no\n  event and no way to stop it. Prefer the wrapped, non-rebasing version (wstETH over stETH).\n- **Blocklists (USDC, USDT).** If the *vault address* is blocklisted, every deposit and withdrawal\n  reverts and funds are frozen until the issuer unblocks it. Nothing onchain can fix this.\n- **Pausable tokens.** Same failure mode, issuer-wide.\n- **Upgradeable tokens.** Today's well-behaved ERC-20 can become a fee-on-transfer or a\n  balance-rewriting token via proxy upgrade. Check who holds the admin key.\n- **Transfer hooks / ERC-777.** A callback token can re-enter. Every entry point is `nonReentrant`\n  (`test_reentrantDepositIsBlocked`, `test_reentrantRedeemIsBlocked`). See \"read-only reentrancy\"\n  below for the part a guard cannot fix.\n- **Weird metadata.** No `symbol()`, `bytes32` symbol (MKR), missing `decimals()`, and hostile\n  symbols containing control characters are all handled — `decimals()` falls back to 18, symbols\n  are sanitised to printable ASCII and capped at 32 bytes. `decimals() > 36` is rejected at\n  construction (it would overflow the receipt token's `decimals()`).\n- **Non-standard returns (USDT).** Handled via `SafeERC20` throughout.\n\n**Seed every new vault yourself.** Right after `createVault`, deposit a small amount and leave it\nthere permanently. It costs almost nothing and removes the empty-vault edge case entirely.\n\n### Running the keeper\n\n- **Use `donate(amount)`, not a bare `transfer`.** Both work identically for accounting, but\n  `donate` measures what actually landed and emits `YieldAdded(from, amount, newTotalAssets)`, which\n  is what you want to index and alert on. A bare transfer is invisible to your indexer.\n- **Never deliver yield into a vault with zero shares outstanding.** `donate` reverts with\n  `NoSharesOutstanding` for exactly this reason, but a bare `transfer` has no such guard — the\n  tokens would be stranded and would wreck the price for the next depositor. Seeding the vault at\n  listing time makes this unreachable.\n- **Approve exact amounts.** The keeper needs `approve(vault, amountForThisDelivery)`, not\n  `type(uint256).max`. A hot keeper key with an infinite approval is a standing drain on whatever\n  account holds the yield float.\n- **Size deliveries relative to TVL.** A single large delivery into a small vault is a\n  sandwich target: deposit immediately before, redeem immediately after. There is no lockup and\n  no fee, so this is free money for a searcher watching the mempool. Mitigations, in order of\n  effectiveness: submit keeper transactions through a private relay (Flashbots Protect) so they\n  are not visible pre-inclusion; deliver frequently in small amounts rather than rarely in large\n  ones; avoid a predictable schedule.\n- **Per-token keeper accounting.** One vault per token, and the vault only ever accepts its own\n  underlying. Sending token X to token Y's vault makes X unrecoverable (there is no rescue\n  function — see below). Key your keeper config off `factory.vaultFor(token)` and verify\n  `vault.asset() == token` before every send.\n- **Watch for silent balance loss.** Because `totalAssets()` is the raw balance, anything that\n  reduces the vault's balance outside a withdrawal (negative rebase, token migration, issuer\n  clawback) shows up as an instant loss for every holder. Alert on `totalAssets()` decreasing by\n  more than the withdrawals in the same block.\n\n---\n\n## Security decisions, and what they cost\n\n### Inflation attack — virtual offset of 1e6\n\nBalance-based accounting means a *donation* is indistinguishable from *yield*, which is the\nmechanism behind the classic ERC-4626 first-depositor attack: deposit 1 wei, donate a large sum,\nand the next depositor's shares round to zero.\n\n`_decimalsOffset() = 6` gives the vault 1e6 virtual shares against 1 virtual asset, so the share\nprice cannot be moved by donation without spending ~1e6× whatever could be extracted. In\n`test_inflationAttackIsNotProfitable` the attacker locks up 100× the victim's deposit, skims\n0.005% of it, and **ends the trade down** — the donation is mostly recovered by the victim, not\nby the attacker. `testFuzz_donationCannotStealFromExistingHolder` fuzzes the general case.\n\nCost: receipt tokens have 6 more decimals than the underlying.\n\n### No owner, no pause, no upgrade, no rescue\n\nDeliberate. There is no admin key, so no one can freeze deposits, block a withdrawal, redirect\nfunds, or upgrade the logic under holders. For a permissionless product where anyone can list\nanything, an admin key that could freeze any vault would be a censorship vector and a single point\nof compromise.\n\n**What this costs — call it out to the builder:**\n\n- No emergency stop. If a listed token turns out to be malicious, the only response is a UI\n  delisting; the vault keeps running.\n- No rescue function. Tokens other than the underlying sent to a vault are **permanently\n  unrecoverable** (`test_noRescueFunctionExists`). A rescue hook would need an owner, and would\n  need to distinguish \"stray token\" from \"the underlying\" — a bug there drains the vault.\n- No fee switch. If the product needs revenue later, that is a new vault version, not an upgrade.\n\nIf the product does need a pause, the right shape is a *deposit-only* pause (never withdrawals)\nbehind a timelock or multisig — not an `onlyOwner` boolean on a hot key.\n\n### Read-only reentrancy\n\n`nonReentrant` protects this contract's state. It does **not** protect *other* protocols that read\nthis vault's price from inside a token callback. During a `deposit` the underlying has already\nlanded but the shares are not minted yet, so `convertToAssets` reads high for the duration of that\nwindow. `isEntered()` is exposed so integrators can detect it:\n\n```solidity\nrequire(!vault.isEntered(), \"vault mid-operation\");\nuint256 value = vault.convertToAssets(shares);\n```\n\nAnything pricing an `svTOKEN` position — a lending market taking it as collateral, say — must\ncheck this. Document it in the integration guide.\n\n### Deliberate ERC-4626 deviations\n\nBoth exist because the spec's guarantees are unachievable for fee-on-transfer tokens, and the\nalternative is a silent loss for existing depositors:\n\n1. `deposit` can return fewer shares than `previewDeposit(assets)` quoted (the fee is charged to\n   the depositor rather than socialised).\n2. `mint` reverts with `InexactMint` rather than minting fewer shares than requested.\n\nFor every well-behaved token, both paths are exactly spec-conformant.\n\n---\n\n## Before mainnet\n\nDone here: CEI + `nonReentrant` on every entry point, `SafeERC20` everywhere, balance-delta\nmeasurement, virtual-share offset, zero-address/zero-amount validation, no infinite approvals in\ncontract code, no admin surface, events on every state change, 26 tests including fuzz and\nadversarial-token mocks.\n\nStill outstanding:\n\n- **Slither / Mythril have not been run** — neither is installed in this environment. Run\n  `slither .` and resolve every reentrancy, unchecked-return, and unprotected-state-change finding\n  before deploying.\n- Longer fuzz campaign (`forge test --fuzz-runs 100000`) and an invariant suite asserting\n  `sum(convertToAssets(balanceOf(holder))) <= totalAssets()` across random action sequences.\n- External audit. The math is small but this contract custodies user funds with no recovery path.\n- Verify the factory on Etherscan after deploy. Vaults are CREATE2-deployed by the factory, so\n  verify one vault and use `predictVault(token)` + the shared bytecode for the rest.\n- Decide and publish the listing policy for the UI: which tokens get shown, who can delist, and\n  what warning a user sees on an unvetted vault. The contracts intentionally do not encode this.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1519,"cache_read_input_tokens":90616,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1519},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"78210e2d-ae8e-4bb2-a869-e8efb63e9f6d","uuid":"bb101cb2-20ff-4d96-aa63-55c75a06bb5a","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:38:52.427Z","request_id":"req_011CdUU5z7V5LhaFam1PgMNu"}

Two contracts:\n\n- `src/SaveVaultFactory.sol` — permissionless registry. Anyone lists any ERC-20, once.\n- `src/SaveVault.sol` — one vault per token. ERC-4626. The receipt token *is* the vault.\n\nDeploy the factory (`script/DeployFactory.s.sol`); everything else happens permissionlessly.\n\n```\nforge build\nforge test\n```\n\n---\n\n## How a depositor's claim is computed\n\n**One sentence:** your shares are a fixed slice of the vault's live token balance, and the keeper\nsending tokens in makes every slice worth more without changing anyone's share count.\n\n### The formula\n\n`totalAssets()` is **the vault's actual ERC-20 balance**, not an internal counter:\n\n```solidity\nfunction totalAssets() public view returns (uint256) {\n    return IERC20(asset()).balanceOf(address(this));\n}\n```\n\nEverything follows from that. Deposits price at the ratio *before* the incoming transfer:\n\n```\nshares  = assetsReceived * (totalSupply + 1e6) / (totalAssetsBefore + 1)     // rounds down\nassets  = shares         * (totalAssets + 1)  / (totalSupply  + 1e6)         // rounds down\n```\n\nThe `+ 1e6` and `+ 1` are **virtual shares and a virtual asset** (`_decimalsOffset() = 6`).\nSee \"Inflation attack\" below — they are load-bearing, not cosmetic.\n\nRounding always favours the vault (i.e. the other depositors), never the caller: shares out round\ndown, shares burned on `withdraw` round up. A depositor can lose at most 1 wei to rounding on a\nround trip, and can never mint value out of thin air. Both properties are fuzzed in\n`testFuzz_noValueCreatedOnRoundTrip`.\n\n### Why yield needs no accounting at all\n\nThe keeper's `transfer` raises `balanceOf(vault)` and therefore `totalAssets()`. `totalSupply()`\ndoes not move. So the claim behind every share rises simultaneously and proportionally. There is\nno reward index, no `accrue()`, no per-user checkpoint, and nothing to migrate when a holder\ntransfers their receipt token — the claim travels with the token because the claim *is* the token.\n\nWorked example (USDC, 6 decimals):\n\n| step                          | totalAssets | totalSupply | alice's claim | bob's claim |\n| ----------------------------- | ----------- | ----------- | ------------- | ----------- |\n| alice deposits 1,000          | 1,000       | 1.0e9 sv    | 1,000         | –           |\n| bob deposits 3,000            | 4,000       | 4.0e9 sv    | 1,000         | 3,000       |\n| keeper transfers in 400       | 4,400       | 4.0e9 sv    | **1,100**     | **3,300**   |\n| bob redeems everything        | 1,100       | 1.0e9 sv    | 1,100         | –           |\n\nYield accrues **only to holders at the time it lands**. A depositor arriving after the transfer\nbuys in at the new, higher price and gets no retroactive share of it\n(`test_lateDepositorDoesNotDiluteEarlierYield`).\n\n### Receipt token shape\n\n`decimals() = underlying.decimals() + 6`. A USDC vault issues 12-decimal `svUSDC`; a DAI vault\nissues 24-decimal `svDAI`. **Do not assume 18, and do not assume it matches the underlying** — the\n`+6` is the virtual-share offset. Name/symbol are derived from the underlying and are *not unique*\n(two tokens can both claim `USDC`). Index vaults by address, never by symbol.\n\n---\n\n## What the operator has to get right\n\n### Listing a token\n\nThe factory's checks are deliberately minimal — reject only what cannot possibly work:\n\n- `token != address(0)`\n- `token.code.length > 0` (no vault over an EOA, or over an address where code might land later)\n- `token.balanceOf(...)` answers (the whole accounting model reads it)\n- no existing vault for that token — CREATE2 with the token as salt makes duplicates impossible\n  even if the registry mapping were bypassed\n\n**Listing is not curation.** Passing those checks says nothing about whether the token is safe to\nhold. The things that will actually bite, in rough order of likelihood:\n\n- **Fee-on-transfer.** Handled: `deposit` mints against the balance delta, so an incoming fee is\n  paid by the depositor, not socialised onto everyone already in the vault\n  (`test_feeOnTransferDepositDoesNotDiluteExistingHolders`). Two consequences to surface in the UI:\n  `previewDeposit` overstates the shares you will get, and `mint` reverts with `InexactMint`\n  (it cannot honour \"exactly N shares\"). Route those tokens through `deposit`. Note many tokens\n  ship with the fee at 0 and a switch to turn it on later — do not decide this at listing time.\n- **Rebasing / balance-changing tokens (stETH, AMPL).** A positive rebase is treated exactly like\n  yield, which is fine. A **negative** rebase silently reduces everyone's claim pro-rata with no\n  event and no way to stop it. Prefer the wrapped, non-rebasing version (wstETH over stETH).\n- **Blocklists (USDC, USDT).** If the *vault address* is blocklisted, every deposit and withdrawal\n  reverts and funds are frozen until the issuer unblocks it. Nothing onchain can fix this.\n- **Pausable tokens.** Same failure mode, issuer-wide.\n- **Upgradeable tokens.** Today's well-behaved ERC-20 can become a fee-on-transfer or a\n  balance-rewriting token via proxy upgrade. Check who holds the admin key.\n- **Transfer hooks / ERC-777.** A callback token can re-enter. Every entry point is `nonReentrant`\n  (`test_reentrantDepositIsBlocked`, `test_reentrantRedeemIsBlocked`). See \"read-only reentrancy\"\n  below for the part a guard cannot fix.\n- **Weird metadata.** No `symbol()`, `bytes32` symbol (MKR), missing `decimals()`, and hostile\n  symbols containing control characters are all handled — `decimals()` falls back to 18, symbols\n  are sanitised to printable ASCII and capped at 32 bytes. `decimals() > 36` is rejected at\n  construction (it would overflow the receipt token's `decimals()`).\n- **Non-standard returns (USDT).** Handled via `SafeERC20` throughout.\n\n**Seed every new vault yourself.** Right after `createVault`, deposit a small amount and leave it\nthere permanently. It costs almost nothing and removes the empty-vault edge case entirely.\n\n### Running the keeper\n\n- **Use `donate(amount)`, not a bare `transfer`.** Both work identically for accounting, but\n  `donate` measures what actually landed and emits `YieldAdded(from, amount, newTotalAssets)`, which\n  is what you want to index and alert on. A bare transfer is invisible to your indexer.\n- **Never deliver yield into a vault with zero shares outstanding.** `donate` reverts with\n  `NoSharesOutstanding` for exactly this reason, but a bare `transfer` has no such guard — the\n  tokens would be stranded and would wreck the price for the next depositor. Seeding the vault at\n  listing time makes this unreachable.\n- **Approve exact amounts.** The keeper needs `approve(vault, amountForThisDelivery)`, not\n  `type(uint256).max`. A hot keeper key with an infinite approval is a standing drain on whatever\n  account holds the yield float.\n- **Size deliveries relative to TVL.** A single large delivery into a small vault is a\n  sandwich target: deposit immediately before, redeem immediately after. There is no lockup and\n  no fee, so this is free money for a searcher watching the mempool. Mitigations, in order of\n  effectiveness: submit keeper transactions through a private relay (Flashbots Protect) so they\n  are not visible pre-inclusion; deliver frequently in small amounts rather than rarely in large\n  ones; avoid a predictable schedule.\n- **Per-token keeper accounting.** One vault per token, and the vault only ever accepts its own\n  underlying. Sending token X to token Y's vault makes X unrecoverable (there is no rescue\n  function — see below). Key your keeper config off `factory.vaultFor(token)` and verify\n  `vault.asset() == token` before every send.\n- **Watch for silent balance loss.** Because `totalAssets()` is the raw balance, anything that\n  reduces the vault's balance outside a withdrawal (negative rebase, token migration, issuer\n  clawback) shows up as an instant loss for every holder. Alert on `totalAssets()` decreasing by\n  more than the withdrawals in the same block.\n\n---\n\n## Security decisions, and what they cost\n\n### Inflation attack — virtual offset of 1e6\n\nBalance-based accounting means a *donation* is indistinguishable from *yield*, which is the\nmechanism behind the classic ERC-4626 first-depositor attack: deposit 1 wei, donate a large sum,\nand the next depositor's shares round to zero.\n\n`_decimalsOffset() = 6` gives the vault 1e6 virtual shares against 1 virtual asset, so the share\nprice cannot be moved by donation without spending ~1e6× whatever could be extracted. In\n`test_inflationAttackIsNotProfitable` the attacker locks up 100× the victim's deposit, skims\n0.005% of it, and **ends the trade down** — the donation is mostly recovered by the victim, not\nby the attacker. `testFuzz_donationCannotStealFromExistingHolder` fuzzes the general case.\n\nCost: receipt tokens have 6 more decimals than the underlying.\n\n### No owner, no pause, no upgrade, no rescue\n\nDeliberate. There is no admin key, so no one can freeze deposits, block a withdrawal, redirect\nfunds, or upgrade the logic under holders. For a permissionless product where anyone can list\nanything, an admin key that could freeze any vault would be a censorship vector and a single point\nof compromise.\n\n**What this costs — call it out to the builder:**\n\n- No emergency stop. If a listed token turns out to be malicious, the only response is a UI\n  delisting; the vault keeps running.\n- No rescue function. Tokens other than the underlying sent to a vault are **permanently\n  unrecoverable** (`test_noRescueFunctionExists`). A rescue hook would need an owner, and would\n  need to distinguish \"stray token\" from \"the underlying\" — a bug there drains the vault.\n- No fee switch. If the product needs revenue later, that is a new vault version, not an upgrade.\n\nIf the product does need a pause, the right shape is a *deposit-only* pause (never withdrawals)\nbehind a timelock or multisig — not an `onlyOwner` boolean on a hot key.\n\n### Read-only reentrancy\n\n`nonReentrant` protects this contract's state. It does **not** protect *other* protocols that read\nthis vault's price from inside a token callback. During a `deposit` the underlying has already\nlanded but the shares are not minted yet, so `convertToAssets` reads high for the duration of that\nwindow. `isEntered()` is exposed so integrators can detect it:\n\n```solidity\nrequire(!vault.isEntered(), \"vault mid-operation\");\nuint256 value = vault.convertToAssets(shares);\n```\n\nAnything pricing an `svTOKEN` position — a lending market taking it as collateral, say — must\ncheck this. Document it in the integration guide.\n\n### Deliberate ERC-4626 deviations\n\nBoth exist because the spec's guarantees are unachievable for fee-on-transfer tokens, and the\nalternative is a silent loss for existing depositors:\n\n1. `deposit` can return fewer shares than `previewDeposit(assets)` quoted (the fee is charged to\n   the depositor rather than socialised).\n2. `mint` reverts with `InexactMint` rather than minting fewer shares than requested.\n\nFor every well-behaved token, both paths are exactly spec-conformant.\n\n---\n\n## Before mainnet\n\nDone here: CEI + `nonReentrant` on every entry point, `SafeERC20` everywhere, balance-delta\nmeasurement, virtual-share offset, zero-address/zero-amount validation, no infinite approvals in\ncontract code, no admin surface, events on every state change, 26 tests including fuzz and\nadversarial-token mocks.\n\nStill outstanding:\n\n- **Slither / Mythril have not been run** — neither is installed in this environment. Run\n  `slither .` and resolve every reentrancy, unchecked-return, and unprotected-state-change finding\n  before deploying.\n- Longer fuzz campaign (`forge test --fuzz-runs 100000`) and an invariant suite asserting\n  `sum(convertToAssets(balanceOf(holder))) <= totalAssets()` across random action sequences.\n- External audit. The math is small but this contract custodies user funds with no recovery path.\n- Verify the factory on Etherscan after deploy. Vaults are CREATE2-deployed by the factory, so\n  verify one vault and use `predictVault(token)` + the shared bytecode for the rest.\n- Decide and publish the listing policy for the UI: which tokens get shown, who can delist, and\n  what warning a user sees on an unvetted vault. The contracts intentionally do not encode this.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}

Mitigations, in order of\n  effectiveness: submit keeper transactions through a private relay (Flashbots Protect) so they\n  are not visible pre-inclusion; deliver frequently in small amounts rather than rarely in large\n  ones; avoid a predictable schedule.\n- **Per-token keeper accounting.** One vault per token, and the vault only ever accepts its own\n  underlying. Sending token X to token Y's vault makes X unrecoverable (there is no rescue\n  function — see below). Key your keeper config off `factory.vaultFor(token)` and verify\n  `vault.asset() == token` before every send.\n- **Watch for silent balance loss.** Because `totalAssets()` is the raw balance, anything that\n  reduces the vault's balance outside a withdrawal (negative rebase, token migration, issuer\n  clawback) shows up as an instant loss for every holder. Alert on `totalAssets()` decreasing by\n  more than the withdrawals in the same block.\n\n---\n\n## Security decisions, and what they cost\n\n### Inflation attack — virtual offset of 1e6\n\nBalance-based accounting means a *donation* is indistinguishable from *yield*, which is the\nmechanism behind the classic ERC-4626 first-depositor attack: deposit 1 wei, donate a large sum,\nand the next depositor's shares round to zero.\n\n`_decimalsOffset() = 6` gives the vault 1e6 virtual shares against 1 virtual asset, so the share\nprice cannot be moved by donation without spending ~1e6× whatever could be extracted. In\n`test_inflationAttackIsNotProfitable` the attacker locks up 100× the victim's deposit, skims\n0.005% of it, and **ends the trade down** — the donation is mostly recovered by the victim, not\nby the attacker. `testFuzz_donationCannotStealFromExistingHolder` fuzzes the general case.\n\nCost: receipt tokens have 6 more decimals than the underlying.\n\n### No owner, no pause, no upgrade, no rescue\n\nDeliberate. There is no admin key, so no one can freeze deposits, block a withdrawal, redirect\nfunds, or upgrade the logic under holders. For a permissionless product where anyone can list\nanything, an admin key that could freeze any vault would be a censorship vector and a single point\nof compromise.\n\n**What this costs — call it out to the builder:**\n\n- No emergency stop. If a listed token turns out to be malicious, the only response is a UI\n  delisting; the vault keeps running.\n- No rescue function. Tokens other than the underlying sent to a vault are **permanently\n  unrecoverable** (`test_noRescueFunctionExists`). A rescue hook would need an owner, and would\n  need to distinguish \"stray token\" from \"the underlying\" — a bug there drains the vault.\n- No fee switch. If the product needs revenue later, that is a new vault version, not an upgrade.\n\nIf the product does need a pause, the right shape is a *deposit-only* pause (never withdrawals)\nbehind a timelock or multisig — not an `onlyOwner` boolean on a hot key.\n\n### Read-only reentrancy\n\n`nonReentrant` protects this contract's state. It does **not** protect *other* protocols that read\nthis vault's price from inside a token callback. During a `deposit` the underlying has already\nlanded but the shares are not minted yet, so `convertToAssets` reads high for the duration of that\nwindow. `isEntered()` is exposed so integrators can detect it:\n\n```solidity\nrequire(!vault.isEntered(), \"vault mid-operation\");\nuint256 value = vault.convertToAssets(shares);\n```\n\nAnything pricing an `svTOKEN` position — a lending market taking it as collateral, say — must\ncheck this. Document it in the integration guide.\n\n### Deliberate ERC-4626 deviations\n\nBoth exist because the spec's guarantees are unachievable for fee-on-transfer tokens, and the\nalternative is a silent loss for existing depositors:\n\n1. `deposit` can return fewer shares than `previewDeposit(assets)` quoted (the fee is charged to\n   the depositor rather than socialised).\n2. `mint` reverts with `InexactMint` rather than minting fewer shares than requested.\n\nFor every well-behaved token, both paths are exactly spec-conformant.\n\n---\n\n## Before mainnet\n\nDone here: CEI + `nonReentrant` on every entry point, `SafeERC20` everywhere, balance-delta\nmeasurement, virtual-share offset, zero-address/zero-amount validation, no infinite approvals in\ncontract code, no admin surface, events on every state change, 26 tests including fuzz and\nadversarial-token mocks.\n\nStill outstanding:\n\n- **Slither / Mythril have not been run** — neither is installed in this environment. Run\n  `slither .` and resolve every reentrancy, unchecked-return, and unprotected-state-change finding\n  before deploying.\n- Longer fuzz campaign (`forge test --fuzz-runs 100000`) and an invariant suite asserting\n  `sum(convertToAssets(balanceOf(holder))) <= totalAssets()` across random action sequences.\n- External audit. The math is small but this contract custodies user funds with no recovery path.\n- Verify the factory on Etherscan after deploy. Vaults are CREATE2-deployed by the factory, so\n  verify one vault and use `predictVault(token)` + the shared bytecode for the rest.\n- Decide and publish the listing policy for the UI: which tokens get shown, who can delist, and\n  what warning a user sees on an unvetted vault. The contracts intentionally do not encode this.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":53,"oldLines":13,"newStart":53,"newLines":15,"lines":[" "," Worked example (USDC, 6 decimals):"," ","-| step                          | totalAssets | totalSupply | alice's claim | bob's claim |","-| ----------------------------- | ----------- | ----------- | ------------- | ----------- |","-| alice deposits 1,000          | 1,000       | 1.0e9 sv    | 1,000         | –           |","-| bob deposits 3,000            | 4,000       | 4.0e9 sv    | 1,000         | 3,000       |","-| keeper transfers in 400       | 4,400       | 4.0e9 sv    | **1,100**     | **3,300**   |","-| bob redeems everything        | 1,100       | 1.0e9 sv    | 1,100         | –           |","+| step                    | totalAssets | totalSupply | alice's claim | bob's claim |","+| ----------------------- | ----------- | ----------- | ------------- | ----------- |","+| alice deposits 1,000    | 1,000       | 1,000 sv    | 1,000         | –           |","+| bob deposits 3,000      | 4,000       | 4,000 sv    | 1,000         | 3,000       |","+| keeper transfers in 400 | 4,400       | 4,000 sv    | **1,100**     | **3,300**   |","+| bob redeems everything  | 1,100       | 1,000 sv    | 1,100         | –           |"," ","+(Amounts in whole tokens; `sv` amounts are 12-decimal, so \"1,000 sv\" is `1e15` raw units.)","+"," Yield accrues **only to holders at the time it lands**. \"../src/SaveVault.sol\";\nimport {SaveVaultFactory} from \"../src/SaveVaultFactory.sol\";\nimport {\n    Bytes32MetadataToken,\n    FeeOnTransferERC20,\n    HostileSymbolToken,\n    MockERC20,\n    NoMetadataNoReturnToken,\n    NotAToken,\n    ReentrantERC20\n} from \"./mocks/Tokens.sol\";\n\ncontract SaveVaultTest is Test {\n    SaveVaultFactory factory;\n    MockERC20 usdc; // 6 decimals, the decimals trap\n    SaveVault vault;\n\n    address alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n    address keeper = makeAddr(\"keeper\");\n    address attacker = makeAddr(\"attacker\");\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        factory = new SaveVaultFactory();\n        usdc = new MockERC20(\"USD Coin\", \"USDC\", 6);\n        vault = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(usdc)));\n\n        for (uint256 i; i < 4; ++i) {\n            address who = [alice, bob, keeper, attacker][i];\n            usdc.mint(who, 1_000_000e6);\n            vm.prank(who);\n            usdc.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Factory\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_factory_deploysAtPredictedAddress() public view {\n        assertEq(factory.vaultFor(address(usdc)), address(vault));\n        assertEq(factory.predictVault(address(usdc)), address(vault));\n        assertEq(factory.vaultCount(), 1);\n        assertEq(vault.asset(), address(usdc));\n        assertEq(vault.factory(), address(factory));\n    }\n\n    function test_factory_rejectsDuplicateListing() public {\n        vm.expectRevert(\n            abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.VaultAlreadyExists.selector, address(usdc), address(vault))\n        );\n        factory.createVault(address(usdc));\n    }\n\n    function test_factory_rejectsZeroAndEoaAndNonToken() public {\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVaultFactory.ZeroAddress.selector);\n        factory.createVault(address(0));\n\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.NotAContract.selector, alice));\n        factory.createVault(alice);\n\n        address notAToken = address(new NotAToken());\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.NotAnERC20.selector, notAToken));\n        factory.createVault(notAToken);\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Receipt token metadata\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_metadata_followsUnderlyingDecimals() public view {\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(vault)).name(), \"Saved USDC\");\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(vault)).symbol(), \"svUSDC\");\n        // 6 (underlying) + 6 (virtual offset)\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(vault)).decimals(), 12);\n    }\n\n    function test_metadata_handlesBytes32Symbol() public {\n        Bytes32MetadataToken mkr = new Bytes32MetadataToken();\n        SaveVault v = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(mkr)));\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(v)).symbol(), \"svMKR\");\n    }\n\n    function test_metadata_handlesMissingMetadata() public {\n        NoMetadataNoReturnToken weird = new NoMetadataNoReturnToken();\n        SaveVault v = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(weird)));\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(v)).symbol(), \"svTKN\");\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(v)).name(), \"Saved Token\");\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(address(v)).decimals(), 24); // 18 fallback + 6\n    }\n\n    function test_metadata_sanitisesHostileSymbol() public {\n        HostileSymbolToken hostile = new HostileSymbolToken();\n        SaveVault v = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(hostile)));\n        string memory symbol_ = IERC20Metadata(address(v)).symbol();\n        // Control bytes dropped, length capped: \"sv\" + 32 sanitised bytes at most.\n        assertLe(bytes(symbol_).length, 34);\n        for (uint256 i; i < bytes(symbol_).length; ++i) {\n            uint8 c = uint8(bytes(symbol_)[i]);\n            assertTrue(c >= 0x20 && c <= 0x7E, \"non-printable byte leaked into symbol\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Core claim math\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function test_deposit_thenRedeemRoundTrip() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), shares);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1_000e6);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 assets = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n\n        assertEq(assets, 1_000e6);\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), 0);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 0);\n    }\n\n    /// Yield is a plain transfer from the keeper. No accrue call, no index update.\n    function test_keeperTransferLiftsEveryClaimProRata() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.deposit(3_000e6, bob);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 400e6); // 10% yield on 4,000\n\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 1_100e6, 1);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 3_300e6, 1);\n    }\n\n    /// A depositor who arrives after the yield does not retroactively share in it.\n    function test_lateDepositorDoesNotDiluteEarlierYield() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 1_000e6); // alice's claim doubles\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.deposit(2_000e6, bob);\n\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 2_000e6, 1);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 2_000e6, 1);\n    }\n\n    function test_donateEmitsAndCreditsHolders() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n\n        vm.expectEmit(true, false, false, true, address(vault));\n        emit SaveVault.YieldAdded(keeper, 100e6, 1_100e6);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        vault.donate(100e6);\n\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 1_100e6, 1);\n    }\n\n    function test_donateRevertsWithNoHolders() public {\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.NoSharesOutstanding.selector);\n        vault.donate(100e6);\n    }\n\n    /// Receipt tokens are transferable and carry the claim with them.\n    function test_sharesAreTransferableClaims() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.transfer(bob, shares);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100e6);\n\n        assertEq(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 0);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 1_100e6, 1);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.redeem(shares, bob, bob);\n        // bob's own 1,000,000 float + alice's 1,000 principal + the 100 of yield\n        assertApproxEqAbs(usdc.balanceOf(bob), 1_001_100e6, 1);\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Inflation / donation attack\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// The classic first-depositor attack: 1 wei deposit, then a fat donation to inflate the\n    /// share price so the victim's deposit rounds to zero shares.\n    function test_inflationAttackIsNotProfitable() public {\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        uint256 attackerShares = vault.deposit(1, attacker);\n\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n
